## P3 - Schema lacks `topology.kinds` entries for `rtbrick_bngblaster`/`bngblaster` despite `additionalProperties: false`

**Location:** [schemas/clab.schema.json:4004-4035](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/fbd18ce0b2e7b230c501440b513189c8e7422441/schemas/clab.schema.json#L4004-L4035)

**Problem:** The PR adds `rtbrick_bngblaster` and `bngblaster` to the kind enum and to the `topology.nodes` definitions, but not to the `topology.kinds` properties section, which closes with `"additionalProperties": false`. The PR&#39;s own test topology uses kind-level config via `topology.kinds.rtbrick_bngblaster` in [`tests/17-rtbrick-bngblaster/01-bngblaster.clab.yml`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/fbd18ce0b2e7b230c501440b513189c8e7422441/tests/17-rtbrick-bngblaster/01-bngblaster.clab.yml#L1-L1) &#40;lines 4-5&#41;.

**Trigger:** A user writes `topology.kinds.rtbrick_bngblaster:` in a topology and validates it with any tooling that consumes [`schemas/clab.schema.json`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/fbd18ce0b2e7b230c501440b513189c8e7422441/schemas/clab.schema.json#L1-L1) &#40;editor validation, schema checks&#41;; the PR&#39;s shipped test topology itself triggers this.

**Impact:** Valid configurations are flagged as invalid by schema-aware tooling, so the new kind cannot be used at kind level without a validation error.

**Suggested correction:** Add `rtbrick_bngblaster` and `bngblaster` property entries under `topology.kinds`, mirroring the shape used in the `topology.nodes` additions &#40;`allOf` referencing `node-config` plus `kind-specific-config-other`&#41;. Note that `veesix_osvbng`, `spirent_stc`, and `ostinato` are also missing from the kinds section, so this is a pre-existing pattern of omission, but this PR adds a new instance and its own test file depends on the missing entry.


## P4 - `PreDeploy` skips `LoadOrGenerateCertificate`, silently ignoring the `certificate` node option

**Location:** [nodes/rtbrick&#95;bngblaster/rtbrick&#95;bngblaster.go:116-133](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/fbd18ce0b2e7b230c501440b513189c8e7422441/nodes/rtbrick_bngblaster/rtbrick_bngblaster.go#L116-L133)

**Problem:** The `bngblaster` `PreDeploy` override neither calls `n.DefaultNode.PreDeploy` &#40;whose only action is `LoadOrGenerateCertificate`, [`nodes/default_node.go:119-128`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/fbd18ce0b2e7b230c501440b513189c8e7422441/nodes/default_node.go#L119-L128)&#41; nor calls `LoadOrGenerateCertificate` explicitly. Comparable kinds retain it&#58; `frr` calls it in its own override &#40;[`nodes/frr/frr.go:183`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/fbd18ce0b2e7b230c501440b513189c8e7422441/nodes/frr/frr.go#L183-L183)&#41;, and `mikrotik_chr` calls `VRNode.PreDeploy`.

**Trigger:** A user sets the generic per-node `certificate:` option on a `bngblaster` node.

**Impact:** The option is silently ignored — no node `certificate` is generated or loaded, with no warning or error.

**Suggested correction:** Call `LoadOrGenerateCertificate` in the override, as `frr` does. This is safe for this root-namespace-based kind because `LoadOrGenerateCertificate` early-returns `nil` when `Cfg.Certificate` is unset or `Issue` is false &#40;[`nodes/default_node.go:894-897`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/fbd18ce0b2e7b230c501440b513189c8e7422441/nodes/default_node.go#L894-L897)&#41;, so it is a no-op unless the user opts in.


## Coverage

- All 26 changed paths from `diff.txt`/`manifest.json` were reviewed&#58; workflows, `README.md`, [`core/register.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/fbd18ce0b2e7b230c501440b513189c8e7422441/core/register.go#L1-L1), the node implementation and its unit tests, [`schemas/clab.schema.json`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/fbd18ce0b2e7b230c501440b513189c8e7422441/schemas/clab.schema.json#L1-L1), docs &#40;kind manual, lab examples, [`mkdocs.yml`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/fbd18ce0b2e7b230c501440b513189c8e7422441/mkdocs.yml#L1-L1) nav&#41;, lab example topologies/JSONs, and the CI test directory.
- Traced surrounding code&#58; destroy/apply flow &#40;[`core/destroy.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/fbd18ce0b2e7b230c501440b513189c8e7422441/core/destroy.go#L1-L1) `PreDestroy` ordering&#41;, docker and podman `StopContainer` handling of the zero-value stop signal, `DefaultNode` `PreDeploy`/`CheckInterfaceName`/`GetEndpoints`, startup-config absolute path resolution &#40;[`core/config.go:524`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/fbd18ce0b2e7b230c501440b513189c8e7422441/core/config.go#L524-L524)&#41;, bind resolution &#40;[`core/config.go:793-826`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/fbd18ce0b2e7b230c501440b513189c8e7422441/core/config.go#L793-L826)&#41;, healthcheck wiring into docker `container.HealthConfig.Test`, and same-node veth link deployment &#40;[`links/link_veth.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/fbd18ce0b2e7b230c501440b513189c8e7422441/links/link_veth.go#L1-L1)&#41;.
- Source-only review&#58; no tests, formatters, or CI were executed. Image-internal details &#40;the healthcheck binary path `/usr/bin/bngblasterctrl` and `bngblaster` CLI semantics&#41; cannot be verified from the repo; the robot test&#39;s `Node Is Healthy` step exercises the healthcheck in CI.
- I did not verify whether the containerlab runtime itself enforces [`schemas/clab.schema.json`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/fbd18ce0b2e7b230c501440b513189c8e7422441/schemas/clab.schema.json#L1-L1) at runtime; the P3 impact is stated for schema-aware tooling and editors, which is the schema&#39;s documented purpose.
- Verified non-issues&#58; `PreDestroy` empty-signal stop defaults, docs claims about PreDestroy-before-link-removal, `LabDir` bind handling, healthcheck `CMD` format, same-node veth links, `eth0` rejection except under `network-mode: none`, workflow/robot/mkdocs conventions, and matching `frr` image tag in lab examples.

<content>
1: ---
2: description: Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Use when writing, reviewing, or refactoring code to avoid overcomplication, make surgical changes, surface assumptions, and define verifiable success criteria.
3: alwaysApply: true
4: ---
5: 
6: # Karpathy behavioral guidelines
7: 
8: Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Merge with project-specific instructions as needed.
9: 
10: **Tradeoff:** These guidelines bias toward caution over speed. For trivial tasks, use judgment.
11: 
12: ## 1. Think Before Coding
13: 
14: **Don't assume. Don't hide confusion. Surface tradeoffs.**
15: 
16: Before implementing:
17: 
18: - State your assumptions explicitly. If uncertain, ask.
19: - If multiple interpretations exist, present them - don't pick silently.
20: - If a simpler approach exists, say so. Push back when warranted.
21: - If something is unclear, stop. Name what's confusing. Ask.
22: 
23: ## 2. Simplicity First
24: 
25: **Minimum code that solves the problem. Nothing speculative.**
26: 
27: - No features beyond what was asked.
28: - No abstractions for single-use code.
29: - No "flexibility" or "configurability" that wasn't requested.
30: - No error handling for impossible scenarios.
31: - If you write 200 lines and it could be 50, rewrite it.
32: 
33: Ask yourself: "Would a senior engineer say this is overcomplicated?" If yes, simplify.
34: 
35: ## 3. Surgical Changes
36: 
37: **Touch only what you must. Clean up only your own mess.**
38: 
39: When editing existing code:
40: 
41: - Don't "improve" adjacent code, comments, or formatting.
42: - Don't refactor things that aren't broken.
43: - Match existing style, even if you'd do it differently.
44: - If you notice unrelated dead code, mention it - don't delete it.
45: 
46: When your changes create orphans:
47: 
48: - Remove imports/variables/functions that YOUR changes made unused.
49: - Don't remove pre-existing dead code unless asked.
50: 
51: The test: Every changed line should trace directly to the user's request.
52: 
53: ## 4. Goal-Driven Execution
54: 
55: **Define success criteria. Loop until verified.**
56: 
57: Transform tasks into verifiable goals:
58: 
59: - "Add validation" → "Write tests for invalid inputs, then make them pass"
60: - "Fix the bug" → "Write a test that reproduces it, then make it pass"
61: - "Refactor X" → "Ensure tests pass before and after"
62: 
63: For multi-step tasks, state a brief plan:
64: 
65: ```
66: 1. [Step] → verify: [check]
67: 2. [Step] → verify: [check]
68: 3. [Step] → verify: [check]
69: ```
70: 
71: Strong success criteria let you loop independently. Weak criteria ("make it work") require constant clarification.
72: 
73: ---
74: 
75: **These guidelines are working if:** fewer unnecessary changes in diffs, fewer rewrites due to overcomplication, and clarifying questions come before implementation rather than after mistakes.

(End of file - total 75 lines)
</content>

1: ---
2: description: Ponytail, lazy senior dev mode. Always pick the simplest solution that works.
3: globs:
4: alwaysApply: true
5: ---
6: 
7: # Ponytail, lazy senior dev mode
8: 
9: You are a lazy senior developer. Lazy means efficient, not careless. The best code is the code never written.
10: 
11: Before writing any code, stop at the first rung that holds:
12: 
13: 1. Does this need to be built at all? (YAGNI)
14: 2. Does it already exist in this codebase? Reuse the helper, util, or pattern that's already here, don't re-write it.
15: 3. Does the standard library already do this? Use it.
16: 4. Does a native platform feature cover it? Use it.
17: 5. Does an already-installed dependency solve it? Use it.
18: 6. Can this be one line? Make it one line.
19: 7. Only then: write the minimum code that works.
20: 
21: The ladder runs after you understand the problem, not instead of it: read the task and the code it touches, trace the real flow end to end, then climb.
22: 
23: Bug fix = root cause, not symptom: a report names a symptom. Grep every caller of the function you touch and fix the shared function once — one guard there is a smaller diff than one per caller, and patching only the path the ticket names leaves a sibling caller still broken.
24: 
25: Rules:
26: 
27: - No abstractions that weren't explicitly requested.
28: - No new dependency if it can be avoided.
29: - No boilerplate nobody asked for.
30: - Deletion over addition. Boring over clever. Fewest files possible.
31: - Shortest working diff wins, but only once you understand the problem. The smallest change in the wrong place isn't lazy, it's a second bug.
32: - Question complex requests: "Do you actually need X, or does Y cover it?"
33: - Pick the edge-case-correct option when two stdlib approaches are the same size, lazy means less code, not the flimsier algorithm.
34: - Mark deliberate simplifications that cut a real corner with a known ceiling (global lock, O(n²) scan, naive heuristic) with a `ponytail:` comment naming the ceiling and upgrade path.
35: 
36: Not lazy about: understanding the problem (read it fully and trace the real flow before picking a rung, a small diff you don't understand is just laziness dressed up as efficiency), input validation at trust boundaries, error handling that prevents data loss, security, accessibility, the calibration real hardware needs (the platform is never the spec ideal, a clock drifts, a sensor reads off), anything explicitly requested. Lazy code without its check is unfinished: non-trivial logic leaves ONE runnable check behind, the smallest thing that fails if the logic breaks (an assert-based demo/self-check or one small test file; no frameworks, no fixtures). Trivial one-liners need no test.

(End of file - total 36 lines)
</content>

191: +|                               |                                                                                    |
192: +| ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
193: +| **Description**               | RtBrick BNG Blaster emulating PPPoE server and clients back to back               |
194: +| **Components**                | [RtBrick BNG Blaster](../manual/kinds/rtbrick_bngblaster.md)                       |
195: +| **Resource requirements**[^1] | :fontawesome-solid-microchip: 1 <br/>:fontawesome-solid-memory: 1 GB               |
196: +| **Topology file**             | [bngblaster01.clab.yml][topofile]                                                  |
197: +| **Name**                      | bngblaster01                                                                       |
198: +
199: +## Description
200: +
201: +A single BNG Blaster node with `eth1` connected to `eth2`. The A10NSP interface `eth1` emulates a PPPoE server and `eth2` the PPPoE clients, so the lab needs no device under test. Replace one side with a BNG to test it.
202: +
203: +The [startup-config](../manual/kinds/rtbrick_bngblaster.md#startup-configuration) `pppoe.json` establishes 10 PPPoE sessions with session traffic and traffic streams, and the test starts automatically once both links are attached. `run.json` enables the report with session and stream details and logging.
204: +
205: +## Use cases
206: +
207: +Follow the test while it is running:
208: +
209: +```bash
210: +docker exec clab-bngblaster01-bngblaster \
211: +  bngblaster-cli /var/bngblaster/clab/run.sock session-counters
212: +```
213: +
214: +or open the web UI at `http://clab-bngblaster01-bngblaster:8001`.
215: +
216: +When the lab is destroyed, the test is stopped and its report is written to `clab-bngblaster01/bngblaster/clab/run_report.json`.
217: +

221: diff --git a/docs/lab-examples/bngblaster02.md b/docs/lab-examples/bngblaster02.md
222: new file mode 100644
223: index 0000000..f34c693
224: --- /dev/null
225: +++ b/docs/lab-examples/bngblaster02.md
226: @@ -0,0 +1,46 @@
227: +|                               |                                                                                    |
228: +| ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
229: +| **Description**               | RtBrick BNG Blaster emulating an IS-IS topology towards FRR, verified with traffic |
230: +| **Components**                | [RtBrick BNG Blaster](../manual/kinds/rtbrick_bngblaster.md), [FRR](../manual/kinds/frr.md) |
231: +| **Resource requirements**[^1] | :fontawesome-solid-microchip: 1 <br/>:fontawesome-solid-memory: 1 GB               |
232: +| **Topology file**             | [bngblaster02.clab.yml][topofile]                                                  |
233: +| **Name**                      | bngblaster02                                                                       |
234: +
235: +## Description
236: +
237: +The BNG Blaster forms an IS-IS level 1 adjacency with FRR on `eth1` and advertises an emulated topology of 20 routers behind it, generated with [lspgen](https://rtbrick.github.io/bngblaster/routing/lspgen.html) and loaded from `isis.mrt`. FRR learns the routes to all emulated routers.
238: +
239: +Two traffic streams are sent from the second BNG Blaster interface `eth2` to the loopback addresses of the emulated routers `node1` (192.168.0.0) and `node20` (192.168.0.11). FRR routes them back to the BNG Blaster on `eth1`, which verifies the streams for loss. The packets sent before FRR installed the routes, usually within a few seconds after the start, are not received.
240: +
241: +```
242: +bngblaster eth1 <---- IS-IS adjacency ----> eth1 frr
243: +bngblaster eth2 ---- traffic streams -----> eth2 frr
244: +```
245: +
246: +The test starts automatically once both links are attached.
247: +
248: +## Use cases
249: +
250: +The IS-IS database and routes of FRR:
251: +
252: +```bash
253: +docker exec clab-bngblaster02-frr vtysh -c "show isis database"
254: +docker exec clab-bngblaster02-frr vtysh -c "show ip route isis"
255: +```
256: +
257: +The adjacency and the traffic streams on the BNG Blaster:
258: +
259: +```bash
260: +docker exec clab-bngblaster02-bngblaster \
261: +  bngblaster-cli /var/bngblaster/clab/run.sock isis-adjacencies
262: +docker exec clab-bngblaster02-bngblaster \
263: +  bngblaster-cli /var/bngblaster/clab/run.sock stream-summary
264: +```
265: +
266: +When the lab is destroyed, the BNG Blaster is stopped first, withdraws its IS-IS topology and closes the adjacency before FRR and the links are removed, and the stream results are written to `clab-bngblaster02/bngblaster/clab/run_report.json`.
267: +
268: +FRR pads its IS-IS hellos to the interface MTU, which is 9500 for containerlab links by default, and sizes its CSNP and PSNP according to it as well. `isis.json` therefore enables `jumbo-frames`, sets the `mtu` of `eth1` to 9500 and raises the IS-IS `max-pdu-size` to 9497 (MTU minus 3 bytes for the LLC header). IS-IS PDUs larger than 1497 bytes are sent as LLC in Ethernet II frames with ethertype 0x8870, see [IS-IS jumbo frames](https://rtbrick.github.io/bngblaster/routing/isis.html#jumbo-frames). This requires BNG Blaster 1.2.0 or newer.
269: +
270: +[topofile]: https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/tree/main/lab-examples/bngblaster02/bngblaster02.clab.yml
271: +
272: +[^1]: Resource requirements are provisional. Consult with the installation guides for additional information.

289: diff --git a/docs/manual/kinds/rtbrick_bngblaster.md b/docs/manual/kinds/rtbrick_bngblaster.md
290: new file mode 100644
291: index 0000000..6e19cc2
292: --- /dev/null
293: +++ b/docs/manual/kinds/rtbrick_bngblaster.md
294: @@ -0,0 +1,139 @@
295: +---
296: +search:
297: +  boost: 4
298: +kind_code_name: rtbrick_bngblaster
299: +kind_display_name: RtBrick BNG Blaster
300: +---
301: +# -{{ kind_display_name }}-
302: +
303: +[-{{ kind_display_name }}-](https://github.com/rtbrick/bngblaster) is an open-source network tester for access and routing protocols. It emulates subscribers (PPPoE, IPoE, L2TP, IPTV) and routing protocols (IS-IS, OSPF, LDP, BGP including EVPN), and verifies millions of traffic streams. -{{ kind_display_name }}- node is identified with the `-{{ kind_code_name }}-` kind in the [topology file](../topo-def-file.md); `bngblaster` is accepted as a short alias.
304: +
305: +The container image runs the [BNG Blaster controller](https://github.com/rtbrick/bngblaster-controller), which manages the test instances and provides a REST API and web UI. Version 1.1.1 or newer of the controller is required, which is part of the image since BNG Blaster 1.1.0. The image `ghcr.io/rtbrick/bngblaster:1.2.0` or newer is recommended.
306: +
307: +## Getting -{{ kind_display_name }}- image
308: +
309: +The image is publicly available in the GitHub Container Registry as [`ghcr.io/rtbrick/bngblaster`](https://github.com/rtbrick/bngblaster/pkgs/container/bngblaster). It is used by default if the node has no `image` configured.
310: +
311: +```bash
312: +docker pull ghcr.io/rtbrick/bngblaster:latest
313: +```
314: +
315: +## Managing -{{ kind_display_name }}- nodes
316: +
317: +/// tab | Web UI and REST API
318: +The controller serves a web UI and REST API on port 8001, from the lab host for example at `http://clab-<lab-name>-<node-name>:8001`. To reach it from a remote browser, publish the port with a different host port per node:
319: +
320: +```yaml
321: +    bngblaster:
322: +      kind: rtbrick_bngblaster
323: +      ports:
324: +        - 8001:8001
325: +```
326: +
327: +///
328: +
329: +/// tab | CLI
330: +`bngblaster-cli` sends commands to the control socket of the running test:
331: +
332: +```bash
333: +docker exec -it clab-<lab-name>-<node-name> \
334: +  bngblaster-cli /var/bngblaster/clab/run.sock session-counters
335: +```
336: +
337: +///
338: +
339: +/// tab | Shell
340: +```bash
341: +docker exec -it clab-<lab-name>-<node-name> bash
342: +```
343: +
344: +///
345: +
346: +## Interface naming
347: +
348: +-{{ kind_display_name }}- uses the interface names of the links as they are, which are referenced in the BNG Blaster configuration:
349: +
350: +* `eth0` - management interface connected to the containerlab management network
351: +* `eth1+` - data interfaces, any other name can be used as well
352: +
353: +## Features and options
354: +
355: +### Startup configuration
356: +
357: +With the [`startup-config`](../nodes.md#startup-config) property, a user sets the path to a BNG Blaster configuration file (JSON). It is copied to `/var/bngblaster/clab/config.json` in the container, and the controller starts this test instance (`clab`) automatically once all links of the node are attached.
358: +
359: +```yaml
360: +topology:
361: +  nodes:
362: +    bngblaster:
363: +      kind: rtbrick_bngblaster
364: +      startup-config: pppoe.json
365: +```
366: +
367: +Without a startup-config, or with [`suppress-startup-config`](../nodes.md#suppress-startup-config), only the controller is started, and tests are created and started through the web UI or REST API.
368: +
369: +As for other kinds, an existing `config.json` from a previous deployment is kept, so changes to the startup-config file take effect only after `containerlab destroy --cleanup`, with `containerlab deploy --reconfigure`, or with [`enforce-startup-config`](../nodes.md#enforce-startup-config) set for the node.
370: +
371: +The start arguments of the test, for example to write a report or log file, are read from `/var/bngblaster/clab/run.json` if present:
372: +
373: +```yaml
374: +      binds:
375: +        - run.json:/var/bngblaster/clab/run.json:ro
376: +```
377: +
378: +```json
379: +{
380: +    "report": true,
381: +    "report_flags": ["sessions", "streams"],
382: +    "logging": true,
383: +    "logging_flags": ["info", "error"]
384: +}
385: +```
386: +
387: +### Results
388: +
389: +The node's lab directory (`clab-<lab-name>/<node-name>`) is mounted as `/var/bngblaster`, the instance directory of the controller. The configuration, logs and the report of the test (`clab/run_report.json`) are kept there after the lab is destroyed, unless the lab directory is removed with `containerlab destroy --cleanup` or `containerlab deploy --reconfigure`.
390: +
391: +### Stopping the test
392: +
393: +The controller stops the test when the container is stopped, and BNG Blaster writes the report in all of the following cases:
394: +
395: +* `containerlab destroy`, with or without `--graceful`, and the removal of the node by `containerlab apply`: the node is stopped before any link or node of the lab is removed, also those of the device under test, so that BNG Blaster tears down its sessions gracefully (PPPoE: LCP Terminate-Request and PADT; routing sessions are closed). A teardown that takes longer than 30 seconds is ended at once, still with the report. For large tests, where the device under test should see every session closed, raise `BNGBLASTERCTRL_STOP_TIMEOUT` (e.g. `5m`) and the containerlab [`--timeout`](../../cmd/deploy.md#timeout) (default 2 minutes) to more than that plus 10 seconds, e.g. `containerlab destroy --timeout 6m`.
396: +
397: +* `containerlab stop`: the links are removed before the node is stopped, so the sessions can not be torn down gracefully. The controller detects the missing interfaces and stops the test at once.
398: +* The test ends by itself or is stopped through the web UI, REST API or `bngblaster-cli`.
399: +
400: +`containerlab start` and `containerlab restart` start the test again once all links are attached. This removes the results of the previous run, so copy them before if needed.
401: +
402: +### Health check
403: +
404: +The node has a default health check, which is healthy while the test is running or after it finished without error, and unhealthy while waiting for the links, while the test starts, or if it failed. Other nodes can therefore wait for the test with [`wait-for`](../nodes.md#stages) and the `healthy` stage. The check is replaced by a [`healthcheck`](../nodes.md#healthcheck) configured for the node.
405: +
406: +### Environment variables
407: +
408: +The kind sets the following controller variables, which can be overridden with the node's `env`:
409: +
410: +| Variable                         | Description                                          | Default                            |
411: +| -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
412: +| `BNGBLASTERCTRL_AUTOSTART`       | Instance started automatically                        | `clab` if a startup-config is set  |
413: +| `BNGBLASTERCTRL_WAIT_INTERFACES` | Number of interfaces to wait for before the start     | number of links of the node        |
414: +
415: +All other controller options are available as `BNGBLASTERCTRL_<OPTION>` variables as well, for example `BNGBLASTERCTRL_STOP_TIMEOUT` (default `30s`) for the graceful teardown when the node is stopped, see the [controller documentation](https://github.com/rtbrick/bngblaster-controller).
416: +
417: +### IPv6
418: +
419: +The kind sets the sysctl `net.ipv6.conf.default.disable_ipv6=1`, so that the kernel does not use IPv6 on the data interfaces, which BNG Blaster handles itself. The management interface keeps IPv6. The sysctl is not set with `network-mode: host` or `network-mode: container:<name>`, where the node has no network namespace of its own.
420: +
421: +## Lab examples
422: +
423: +* [BNG Blaster PPPoE](../../lab-examples/bngblaster01.md) - PPPoE server and clients emulated back to back by one BNG Blaster node.
424: +* [BNG Blaster and FRR IS-IS](../../lab-examples/bngblaster02.md) - emulated IS-IS topology advertised to FRR, verified with traffic streams through FRR.
425: +
426: +## Known issues and limitations
427: +
428: +* containerlab links have an MTU of 9500 by default, while BNG Blaster network interfaces use an MTU of 1500 by default and IS-IS accepts PDUs of up to 1497 bytes. Routers size IS-IS PDUs to the link MTU, for example padded hellos, and depending on the implementation LSPs and CSNPs, which are then rejected, so that the adjacency does not come up or the database is incomplete. Either configure `jumbo-frames`, the `mtu` of the interface and the IS-IS `max-pdu-size` of the BNG Blaster according to the link MTU, as in the [IS-IS lab example](../../lab-examples/bngblaster02.md) (requires BNG Blaster 1.2.0 or newer), or set the [`mtu`](../topo-def-file.md#links) of links to routing peers to 1500.
429: +* Without `"interfaces": {"jumbo-frames": true}` in the BNG Blaster configuration, frames larger than about 4 KB are not received completely.
430: +
431: +## Contact
432: +
433: +The kind is maintained by RtBrick, contact <bngblaster@rtbrick.com>.

694: new file mode 100644
695: index 0000000..31d004f
696: --- /dev/null
697: +++ b/nodes/rtbrick_bngblaster/rtbrick_bngblaster.go
698: @@ -0,0 +1,184 @@
699: +// Copyright 2026 RtBrick, Inc.
700: +// Licensed under the BSD 3-Clause License.
701: +// SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
702: +
703: +package rtbrick_bngblaster
704: +
705: +import (
706: +	"context"
707: +	"fmt"
708: +	"os"
709: +	"path"
710: +	"strconv"
711: +	"strings"
712: +
713: +	clabconstants "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/constants"
714: +	clabnodes "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/nodes"
715: +	clabruntime "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/runtime"
716: +	clabtypes "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/types"
717: +	clabutils "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/utils"
718: +)
719: +
720: +var kindNames = []string{"rtbrick_bngblaster", "bngblaster"}
721: +
722: +const (
723: +	generateable     = true
724: +	generateIfFormat = "eth%d"
725: +
726: +	// DefaultImage is used if the node has no image configured.
727: +	DefaultImage = "ghcr.io/rtbrick/bngblaster:latest"
728: +
729: +	// instanceDir is the BNG Blaster controller config folder in the container,
730: +	// bound to the node's lab directory, so that the logs and reports of the
731: +	// test are kept in the lab directory.
732: +	instanceDir = "/var/bngblaster"
733: +	// instanceName is the controller instance started from the startup-config.
734: +	instanceName = "clab"
735: +	configFile   = "config.json"
736: +
737: +	envAutostart      = "BNGBLASTERCTRL_AUTOSTART"
738: +	envWaitInterfaces = "BNGBLASTERCTRL_WAIT_INTERFACES"
739: +
740: +	// sysctlDisableIPv6 disables IPv6 on the data interfaces, which containerlab
741: +	// attaches after the container started. Not net.ipv6.conf.all, which would
742: +	// also overwrite the default and disable IPv6 on the management interface.
743: +	sysctlDisableIPv6 = "net.ipv6.conf.default.disable_ipv6"
744: +)
745: +
746: +// defaultHealthcheck reports the node healthy while the test runs or after it
747: +// finished without error. It is unhealthy while the controller waits for the
748: +// links (up to 5 minutes by default), which the start period covers.
749: +var defaultHealthcheck = clabtypes.HealthcheckConfig{
750: +	Test:        []string{"CMD", "/usr/bin/bngblasterctrl", "-health"},
751: +	Interval:    5,
752: +	Timeout:     3,
753: +	Retries:     3,
754: +	StartPeriod: 300,
755: +}
756: +
757: +// Register registers the node in the NodeRegistry.
758: +func Register(r *clabnodes.NodeRegistry) {
759: +	generateNodeAttributes := clabnodes.NewGenerateNodeAttributes(generateable, generateIfFormat)
760: +	nrea := clabnodes.NewNodeRegistryEntryAttributes(nil, generateNodeAttributes, nil)
761: +
762: +	r.Register(kindNames, func() clabnodes.Node {
763: +		return new(bngblaster)
764: +	}, nrea)
765: +}
766: +
767: +type bngblaster struct {
768: +	clabnodes.DefaultNode
769: +}
770: +
771: +func (n *bngblaster) Init(cfg *clabtypes.NodeConfig, opts ...clabnodes.NodeOption) error {
772: +	n.DefaultNode = *clabnodes.NewDefaultNode(n)
773: +	n.Cfg = cfg
774: +
775: +	if n.Cfg.Image == "" {
776: +		n.Cfg.Image = DefaultImage
777: +	}
778: +
779: +	if n.Cfg.Env == nil {
780: +		n.Cfg.Env = map[string]string{}
781: +	}
782: +	if n.Cfg.StartupConfig != "" {
783: +		n.Cfg.ResStartupConfig = path.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, instanceName, configFile)
784: +		// A suppressed startup-config is not written, so there is no config
785: +		// to start the instance with.
786: +		if !n.Cfg.SuppressStartupConfig {
787: +			setDefault(n.Cfg.Env, envAutostart, instanceName)
788: +		}
789: +	}
790: +
791: +	// The node has no network namespace of its own with network-mode host or
792: +	// container:<name>, where the runtime rejects net.* sysctls.
793: +	if hasOwnNetns(n.Cfg.NetworkMode) {
794: +		if n.Cfg.Sysctls == nil {
795: +			n.Cfg.Sysctls = map[string]string{}
796: +		}
797: +		setDefault(n.Cfg.Sysctls, sysctlDisableIPv6, "1")
798: +	}
799: +
800: +	if n.Cfg.Healthcheck == nil {
801: +		hc := defaultHealthcheck
802: +		n.Cfg.Healthcheck = &hc
803: +	}
804: +
805: +	n.Cfg.Binds = append(n.Cfg.Binds, n.Cfg.LabDir+":"+instanceDir)
806: +
807: +	for _, o := range opts {
808: +		o(n)
809: +	}
810: +
811: +	return nil
812: +}
813: +
814: +func (n *bngblaster) PreDeploy(ctx context.Context, _ *clabnodes.PreDeployParams) error {
815: +	clabutils.CreateDirectory(n.Cfg.LabDir, clabconstants.PermissionsOpen)
816: +
817: +	if n.Cfg.StartupConfig == "" {
818: +		return nil
819: +	}
820: +
821: +	clabutils.CreateDirectory(path.Dir(n.Cfg.ResStartupConfig), clabconstants.PermissionsOpen)
822: +
823: +	cfg, err := os.ReadFile(n.Cfg.StartupConfig)
824: +	if err != nil {
825: +		return err
826: +	}
827: +
828: +	return n.GenerateConfig(ctx, n.Cfg.ResStartupConfig, string(cfg))
829: +}
830: +
831: +// Deploy lets the controller wait for all links before it starts the test.
832: +func (n *bngblaster) Deploy(ctx context.Context, params *clabnodes.DeployParams) error {
833: +	if n.Cfg.Env[envAutostart] != "" {
834: +		setDefault(n.Cfg.Env, envWaitInterfaces, strconv.Itoa(len(n.GetEndpoints())))
835: +	}
836: +
837: +	return n.DefaultNode.Deploy(ctx, params)
838: +}
839: +
840: +// PreDestroy stops the container on destroy and apply. It runs before any link
841: +// or node of the lab is removed, also those of the device under test, so that
842: +// BNG Blaster can tear down its sessions over the links and write the report of
843: +// the test. On SIGTERM the controller stops the test gracefully and ends the
844: +// teardown at once after BNGBLASTERCTRL_STOP_TIMEOUT (default 30s), still with
845: +// the report. The container is removed afterwards anyway, also if it did not
846: +// stop, so a failed stop is not an error.
847: +func (n *bngblaster) PreDestroy(ctx context.Context) error {
848: +	if n.GetContainerStatus(ctx) == clabruntime.Running {
849: +		_ = n.Runtime.StopContainer(ctx, n.GetContainerName(), n.StopSignal)
850: +	}
851: +
852: +	return nil
853: +}
854: +
855: +// CheckInterfaceName allows any interface name, except eth0 when the
856: +// management interface uses it.
857: +func (n *bngblaster) CheckInterfaceName() error {
858: +	nm := strings.ToLower(n.Cfg.NetworkMode)
859: +	for _, e := range n.Endpoints {
860: +		if e.GetIfaceName() == "eth0" && nm != "none" {
861: +			return fmt.Errorf(
862: +				"eth0 interface name is not allowed for %s node when network mode is not set to none",
863: +				n.Cfg.ShortName,
864: +			)
865: +		}
866: +	}
867: +
868: +	return n.CheckInterfaceOverlap()
869: +}
870: +
871: +// hasOwnNetns reports whether the node has a network namespace of its own.
872: +func hasOwnNetns(networkMode string) bool {
873: +	nm := strings.ToLower(networkMode)
874: +
875: +	return nm != "host" && !strings.HasPrefix(nm, "container:")
876: +}
877: +
878: +func setDefault(m map[string]string, key, value string) {
879: +	if _, ok := m[key]; !ok {
880: +		m[key] = value
881: +	}
882: +}

1023: +func TestDeployWaitInterfaces(t *testing.T) {
1024: +	endpoints := []clablinks.Endpoint{
1025: +		&clablinks.EndpointVeth{EndpointGeneric: clablinks.EndpointGeneric{IfaceName: "eth1"}},
1026: +		&clablinks.EndpointVeth{EndpointGeneric: clablinks.EndpointGeneric{IfaceName: "eth2"}},
1027: +	}
1028: +
1029: +	tests := map[string]struct {
1030: +		env  map[string]string
1031: +		want string
1032: +	}{
1033: +		"links counted with autostart": {env: map[string]string{envAutostart: "clab"}, want: "2"},
1034: +		"user value wins": {
1035: +			env:  map[string]string{envAutostart: "clab", envWaitInterfaces: "1"},
1036: +			want: "1",
1037: +		},
1038: +		"no wait without autostart":    {env: map[string]string{}, want: ""},
1039: +		"no wait with empty autostart": {env: map[string]string{envAutostart: ""}, want: ""},
1040: +	}
1041: +
1042: +	for name, tc := range tests {
1043: +		t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
1044: +			rt := clabmocksmockruntime.NewMockContainerRuntime(gomock.NewController(t))
1045: +			n := new(bngblaster)
1046: +			if err := n.Init(
1047: +				&clabtypes.NodeConfig{Env: tc.env},
1048: +				clabnodes.WithRuntime(rt),
1049: +			); err != nil {
1050: +				t.Fatal(err)
1051: +			}
1052: +			n.Endpoints = endpoints
1053: +
1054: +			rt.EXPECT().CreateContainer(gomock.Any(), gomock.Any()).DoAndReturn(
1055: +				func(_ context.Context, cfg *clabtypes.NodeConfig) (string, error) {
1056: +					if got := cfg.Env[envWaitInterfaces]; got != tc.want {
1057: +						t.Errorf("%s = %q, want %q", envWaitInterfaces, got, tc.want)
1058: +					}
1059: +					return "id", nil
1060: +				})
1061: +			rt.EXPECT().StartContainer(gomock.Any(), "id", gomock.Any())
1062: +
1063: +			if err := n.Deploy(context.Background(), &clabnodes.DeployParams{}); err != nil {
1064: +				t.Fatal(err)
1065: +			}
1066: +		})
1067: +	}
1068: +}

1070: +func TestPreDestroyStopsContainer(t *testing.T) {
1071: +	tests := map[string]struct {
1072: +		status   clabruntime.ContainerStatus
1073: +		wantStop bool
1074: +	}{
1075: +		"running container is stopped":       {status: clabruntime.Running, wantStop: true},
1076: +		"stopped container is left as it is": {status: clabruntime.Stopped, wantStop: false},
1077: +	}
1078: +
1079: +	for name, tc := range tests {
1080: +		t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {

1082: +			n := new(bngblaster)
1083: +			cfg := &clabtypes.NodeConfig{LongName: "clab-lab-bbl"}
1084: +			if err := n.Init(cfg, clabnodes.WithRuntime(rt)); err != nil {
1085: +				t.Fatal(err)
1086: +			}
1087: +
1088: +			rt.EXPECT().GetContainerStatus(gomock.Any(), "clab-lab-bbl").Return(tc.status)
1089: +			if tc.wantStop {
1090: +				// A failed stop is not an error, the container is removed anyway.
1091: +				rt.EXPECT().StopContainer(gomock.Any(), "clab-lab-bbl", gomock.Any()).
1092: +					Return(errors.New("stop failed"))
1093: +			}
1094: +
1095: +			if err := n.PreDestroy(context.Background()); err != nil {
1096: +				t.Fatal(err)
1097: +			}
1098: +		})
1099: +	}
1100: +}

1230: +*** Settings ***

1245: +
1246: +
1247: +*** Test Cases ***
1248: +Startup configuration starts the test once all links are attached
1249: +    ${config} =    Get File    ${lab-dir}/pppoe/clab/config.json
1250: +    Should Contain    ${config}    "type": "pppoe"
1251: +    ${env} =    Node Command    pppoe    env
1252: +    Should Contain    ${env}    BNGBLASTERCTRL_AUTOSTART=clab
1253: +    Should Contain    ${env}    BNGBLASTERCTRL_WAIT_INTERFACES=2
1254: +    ${env} =    Node Command    isis1    env
1255: +    Should Contain    ${env}    BNGBLASTERCTRL_WAIT_INTERFACES=2
1256: +
1257: +Nodes report healthy
1258: +    FOR    ${node}    IN    pppoe    isis1    isis2    ctrl
1259: +        Wait Until Keyword Succeeds    120s    2s    Node Is Healthy    ${node}
1260: +    END
1261: +
1262: +PPPoE sessions are established and their traffic is verified
1263: +    Wait Until Keyword Succeeds    60s    2s    Session Counters Contain    "sessions-established": 10
1264: +    Wait Until Keyword Succeeds    60s    2s    Session Counters Contain    "session-traffic-flows-verified": 20
1265: +    Wait Until Keyword Succeeds    60s    2s    Session Counters Contain    "stream-traffic-flows-verified": 20
1266: +
1267: +IS-IS adjacency between two nodes comes up
1268: +    Wait Until Keyword Succeeds    60s    2s    IS-IS Adjacency Is Up    isis1    0100.0000.0002
1269: +    Wait Until Keyword Succeeds    60s    2s    IS-IS Adjacency Is Up    isis2    0100.0000.0001
1270: +
1271: +Alias without startup-config only starts the controller
1272: +    ${env} =    Node Command    ctrl    env
1273: +    Should Not Contain    ${env}    BNGBLASTERCTRL_AUTOSTART
1274: +    Should Not Contain    ${env}    BNGBLASTERCTRL_WAIT_INTERFACES
1275: +    Directory Should Not Exist    ${lab-dir}/ctrl/clab
1276: +
1277: +IPv6 is disabled on data interfaces only
1278: +    ${data} =    Node Command    isis1    cat /proc/sys/net/ipv6/conf/eth1/disable_ipv6
1279: +    Should Be Equal    ${data}    1
1280: +    ${mgmt} =    Node Command    isis1    cat /proc/sys/net/ipv6/conf/eth0/disable_ipv6
1281: +    Should Be Equal    ${mgmt}    0
1282: +
1283: +Destroy tears the test down gracefully and keeps the report
1284: +    Clab Command    destroy -t ${topology}
1285: +    # SIGINT means the links were still present when the node was stopped;
1286: +    # the controller uses SIGTERM at once if they are already gone.
1287: +    ${log} =    Get File    ${lab-dir}/pppoe/clab/run.log
1288: +    Should Contain    ${log}    Received signal Interrupt
1289: +    Should Contain    ${log}    ALL SESSIONS TERMINATED
1290: +    ${report} =    Get File    ${lab-dir}/pppoe/clab/run_report.json
1291: +    Should Contain    ${report}    "sessions-established": 10

1293: +    # a device under test does, so isis1 must be stopped before any node of
1294: +    # the lab is deleted.

/dev/null\n189: +++ b/docs/lab-examples/bngblaster01.md\n190: @@ -0,0 +1,30 @@\n191: +|                               | requirements**[^1] | :fontawesome-solid-microchip: 1 <br/>:fontawesome-solid-memory: 1 GB               |\n196: +| **Topology file**             | [bngblaster01.clab.yml][topofile]                                                  |\n197: +| **Name**                      | bngblaster01                                                                       |\n198: +\n199: +## Description\n200: +\n201: +A single BNG Blaster node with `eth1` connected to `eth2`. The A10NSP interface `eth1` emulates a PPPoE server and `eth2` the PPPoE clients, so the lab needs no device under test. Replace one side with a BNG to test it.\n202: +\n203: +The [startup-config](../manual/kinds/rtbrick_bngblaster.md#startup-configuration) `pppoe.json` establishes 10 PPPoE sessions with session traffic and traffic streams, and the test starts automatically once both links are attached. `run.json` enables the report with session and stream details and logging.\n204: +\n205: +## Use cases\n206: +\n207: +Follow the test while it is running:\n208: +\n209: +```bash\n210: +docker exec clab-bngblaster01-bngblaster \\\n211: +  bngblaster-cli /var/bngblaster/clab/run.sock session-counters\n212: +```\n213: +\n214: +or open the web UI at `http://clab-bngblaster01-bngblaster:8001`.\n215: +\n216: +When the lab is destroyed, the test is stopped and its report is written to `clab-bngblaster01/bngblaster/clab/run_report.json`.\n217: +\n218: +[topofile]: https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/tree/main/lab-examples/bngblaster01/bngblaster01.clab.yml\n219: +\n220: +[^1]: Resource requirements are provisional. Consult with the installation guides for additional information.\n221: diff --git a/docs/lab-examples/bngblaster02.md b/docs/lab-examples/bngblaster02.md\n222: new file mode 100644\n223: index 0000000..f34c693\n224: --- /dev/null\n225: +++ b/docs/lab-examples/bngblaster02.md\n226: @@ -0,0 +1,46 @@\n227: +|                               |                                                                                    |\n228: +| ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n229: +| **Description**               | RtBrick BNG Blaster emulating an IS-IS topology towards FRR, verified with traffic |\n230: +| **Components**                | [RtBrick BNG Blaster](../manual/kinds/rtbrick_bngblaster.md), [FRR](../manual/kinds/frr.md) |\n231: +| **Resource requirements**[^1] | :fontawesome-solid-microchip: 1 <br/>:fontawesome-solid-memory: 1 GB               |\n232: +| **Topology file**             | [bngblaster02.clab.yml][topofile]                                                  |\n233: +| **Name**                      | bngblaster02                                                                       |\n234: +\n235: +## Description\n236: +\n237: +The BNG Blaster forms an IS-IS level 1 adjacency with FRR on `eth1` and advertises an emulated topology of 20 routers behind it, generated with [lspgen](https://rtbrick.github.io/bngblaster/routing/lspgen.html) and loaded from `isis.mrt`. FRR learns the routes to all emulated routers.\n238: +\n239: +Two traffic streams are sent from the second BNG Blaster interface `eth2` to the loopback addresses of the emulated routers `node1` (192.168.0.0) and `node20` (192.168.0.11). FRR routes them back to the BNG Blaster on `eth1`, which verifies the streams for loss. The packets sent before FRR installed the routes, usually within a few seconds after the start, are not received.\n240: +\n241: +```\n242: +bngblaster eth1 <---- IS-IS adjacency ----> eth1 frr\n243: +bngblaster eth2 ---- traffic streams -----> eth2 frr\n244: +```\n245: +\n246: +The test starts automatically once both links are attached.\n247: +\n248: +## Use cases\n249: +\n250: +The IS-IS database and routes of FRR:\n251: +\n252: +```bash\n253: +docker exec clab-bngblaster02-frr vtysh -c \"show isis database\"\n254: +docker exec clab-bngblaster02-frr vtysh -c \"show ip route isis\"\n255: +```\n256: +\n257: +The adjacency and the traffic streams on the BNG Blaster:\n258: +\n259: +```bash\n260: +docker exec clab-bngblaster02-bngblaster \\\n261: +  bngblaster-cli /var/bngblaster/clab/run.sock isis-adjacencies\n262: +docker exec clab-bngblaster02-bngblaster \\\n263: +  bngblaster-cli /var/bngblaster/clab/run.sock stream-summary\n264: +```\n265: +\n266: +When the lab is destroyed, the BNG Blaster is stopped first, withdraws its IS-IS topology and closes the adjacency before FRR and the links are removed, and the stream results are written to `clab-bngblaster02/bngblaster/clab/run_report.json`.\n267: +\n268: +FRR pads its IS-IS hellos to the interface MTU, which is 9500 for containerlab links by default, and sizes its CSNP and PSNP according to it as well. `isis.json` therefore enables `jumbo-frames`, sets the `mtu` of `eth1` to 9500 and raises the IS-IS `max-pdu-size` to 9497 (MTU minus 3 bytes for the LLC header). IS-IS PDUs larger than 1497 bytes are sent as LLC in Ethernet II frames with ethertype 0x8870, see [IS-IS jumbo frames](https://rtbrick.github.io/bngblaster/routing/isis.html#jumbo-frames). This requires BNG Blaster 1.2.0 or newer.\n269: +\n270: +[topofile]: https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/tree/main/lab-examples/bngblaster02/bngblaster02.clab.yml\n271: +\n272: +[^1]: Resource requirements are provisional. b/docs/manual/kinds/rtbrick_bngblaster.md\n290: new file mode 100644\n291: index 0000000..6e19cc2\n292: --- /dev/null\n293: +++ b/docs/manual/kinds/rtbrick_bngblaster.md\n294: @@ -0,0 +1,139 @@\n295: +---\n296: +search:\n297: +  boost: 4\n298: +kind_code_name: rtbrick_bngblaster\n299: +kind_display_name: RtBrick BNG Blaster\n300: +---\n301: +# -{{ kind_display_name }}-\n302: +\n303: +[-{{ kind_display_name }}-](https://github.com/rtbrick/bngblaster) is an open-source network tester for access and routing protocols. It emulates subscribers (PPPoE, IPoE, L2TP, IPTV) and routing protocols (IS-IS, OSPF, LDP, BGP including EVPN), and verifies millions of traffic streams. -{{ kind_display_name }}- node is identified with the `-{{ kind_code_name }}-` kind in the [topology file](../topo-def-file.md); `bngblaster` is accepted as a short alias.\n304: +\n305: +The container image runs the [BNG Blaster controller](https://github.com/rtbrick/bngblaster-controller), which manages the test instances and provides a REST API and web UI. Version 1.1.1 or newer of the controller is required, which is part of the image since BNG Blaster 1.1.0. The image `ghcr.io/rtbrick/bngblaster:1.2.0` or newer is recommended.\n306: +\n307: +## Getting -{{ kind_display_name }}- image\n308: +\n309: +The image is publicly available in the GitHub Container Registry as [`ghcr.io/rtbrick/bngblaster`](https://github.com/rtbrick/bngblaster/pkgs/container/bngblaster). It is used by default if the node has no `image` configured.\n310: +\n311: +```bash\n312: +docker pull ghcr.io/rtbrick/bngblaster:latest\n313: +```\n314: +\n315: +## Managing -{{ kind_display_name }}- nodes\n316: +\n317: +/// tab | Web UI and REST API\n318: +The controller serves a web UI and REST API on port 8001, from the lab host for example at `http://clab-<lab-name>-<node-name>:8001`. To reach it from a remote browser, publish the port with a different host port per node:\n319: +\n320: +```yaml\n321: +    bngblaster:\n322: +      kind: rtbrick_bngblaster\n323: +      ports:\n324: +        - 8001:8001\n325: +```\n326: +\n327: +///\n328: +\n329: +/// tab | CLI\n330: +`bngblaster-cli` sends commands to the control socket of the running test:\n331: +\n332: +```bash\n333: +docker exec -it clab-<lab-name>-<node-name> \\\n334: +  bngblaster-cli /var/bngblaster/clab/run.sock session-counters\n335: +```\n336: +\n337: +///\n338: +\n339: +/// tab | Shell\n340: +```bash\n341: +docker exec -it clab-<lab-name>-<node-name> bash\n342: +```\n343: +\n344: +///\n345: +\n346: +## Interface naming\n347: +\n348: +-{{ kind_display_name }}- uses the interface names of the links as they are, which are referenced in the BNG Blaster configuration:\n349: +\n350: +* `eth0` - management interface connected to the containerlab management network\n351: +* `eth1+` - data interfaces, any other name can be used as well\n352: +\n353: +## Features and options\n354: +\n355: +### Startup configuration\n356: +\n357: +With the [`startup-config`](../nodes.md#startup-config) property, a user sets the path to a BNG Blaster configuration file (JSON). It is copied to `/var/bngblaster/clab/config.json` in the container, and the controller starts this test instance (`clab`) automatically once all links of the node are attached.\n358: +\n359: +```yaml\n360: +topology:\n361: +  nodes:\n362: +    bngblaster:\n363: +      kind: rtbrick_bngblaster\n364: +      startup-config: pppoe.json\n365: +```\n366: +\n367: +Without a startup-config, or with [`suppress-startup-config`](../nodes.md#suppress-startup-config), only the controller is started, and tests are created and started through the web UI or REST API.\n368: +\n369: +As for other kinds, an existing `config.json` from a previous deployment is kept, so changes to the startup-config file take effect only after `containerlab destroy --cleanup`, with `containerlab deploy --reconfigure`, or with [`enforce-startup-config`](../nodes.md#enforce-startup-config) set for the node.\n370: +\n371: +The start arguments of the test, for example to write a report or log file, are read from `/var/bngblaster/clab/run.json` if present:\n372: +\n373: +```yaml\n374: +      binds:\n375: +        - run.json:/var/bngblaster/clab/run.json:ro\n376: +```\n377: +\n378: +```json\n379: +{\n380: +    \"report\": true,\n381: +    \"report_flags\": [\"sessions\", \"streams\"],\n382: +    \"logging\": true,\n383: +    \"logging_flags\": [\"info\", \"error\"]\n384: +}\n385: +```\n386: +\n387: +### Results\n388: +\n389: +The node's lab directory (`clab-<lab-name>/<node-name>`) is mounted as `/var/bngblaster`, the instance directory of the controller. The configuration, logs and the report of the test (`clab/run_report.json`) are kept there after the lab is destroyed, unless the lab directory is removed with `containerlab destroy --cleanup` or `containerlab deploy --reconfigure`.\n390: +\n391: +### Stopping the test\n392: +\n393: +The controller stops the test when the container is stopped, and BNG Blaster writes the report in all of the following cases:\n394: +\n395: +* `containerlab destroy`, with or without `--graceful`, and the removal of the node by `containerlab apply`: the node is stopped before any link or node of the lab is removed, also those of the device under test, so that BNG Blaster tears down its sessions gracefully (PPPoE: LCP Terminate-Request and PADT; routing sessions are closed). A teardown that takes longer than 30 seconds is ended at once, still with the report. For large tests, where the device under test should see every session closed, raise `BNGBLASTERCTRL_STOP_TIMEOUT` (e.g. `5m`) and the containerlab [`--timeout`](../../cmd/deploy.md#timeout) (default 2 minutes) to more than that plus 10 seconds, e.g. `containerlab destroy --timeout 6m`.\n396: +\n397: +* `containerlab stop`: the links are removed before the node is stopped, so the sessions can not be torn down gracefully. The controller detects the missing interfaces and stops the test at once.\n398: +* The test ends by itself or is stopped through the web UI, REST API or `bngblaster-cli`.\n399: +\n400: +`containerlab start` and `containerlab restart` start the test again once all links are attached. This removes the results of the previous run, so copy them before if needed.\n401: +\n402: +### Health check\n403: +\n404: +The node has a default health check, which is healthy while the test is running or after it finished without error, and unhealthy while waiting for the links, while the test starts, or if it failed. Other nodes can therefore wait for the test with [`wait-for`](../nodes.md#stages) and the `healthy` stage. The check is replaced by a [`healthcheck`](../nodes.md#healthcheck) configured for the node.\n405: +\n406: +### Environment variables\n407: +\n408: +The kind sets the following controller variables, which can be overridden with the node's `env`:\n409: +\n410: +| Variable                         | Description                                          | Default                            |\n411: +| -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |\n412: +| `BNGBLASTERCTRL_AUTOSTART`       | Instance started automatically                        | `clab` if a startup-config is set  |\n413: +| `BNGBLASTERCTRL_WAIT_INTERFACES` | Number of interfaces to wait for before the start     | number of links of the node        |\n414: +\n415: +All other controller options are available as `BNGBLASTERCTRL_<OPTION>` variables as well, for example `BNGBLASTERCTRL_STOP_TIMEOUT` (default `30s`) for the graceful teardown when the node is stopped, see the [controller documentation](https://github.com/rtbrick/bngblaster-controller).\n416: +\n417: +### IPv6\n418: +\n419: +The kind sets the sysctl `net.ipv6.conf.default.disable_ipv6=1`, so that the kernel does not use IPv6 on the data interfaces, which BNG Blaster handles itself. The management interface keeps IPv6. The sysctl is not set with `network-mode: host` or `network-mode: container:<name>`, where the node has no network namespace of its own.\n420: +\n421: +## Lab examples\n422: +\n423: +* [BNG Blaster PPPoE](../../lab-examples/bngblaster01.md) - PPPoE server and clients emulated back to back by one BNG Blaster node.\n424: +* [BNG Blaster and FRR IS-IS](../../lab-examples/bngblaster02.md) - emulated IS-IS topology advertised to FRR, verified with traffic streams through FRR.\n425: +\n426: +## Known issues and limitations\n427: +\n428: +* containerlab links have an MTU of 9500 by default, while BNG Blaster network interfaces use an MTU of 1500 by default and IS-IS accepts PDUs of up to 1497 bytes. Routers size IS-IS PDUs to the link MTU, for example padded hellos, and depending on the implementation LSPs and CSNPs, which are then rejected, so that the adjacency does not come up or the database is incomplete. Either configure `jumbo-frames`, the `mtu` of the interface and the IS-IS `max-pdu-size` of the BNG Blaster according to the link MTU, as in the [IS-IS lab example](../../lab-examples/bngblaster02.md) (requires BNG Blaster 1.2.0 or newer), or set the [`mtu`](../topo-def-file.md#links) of links to routing peers to 1500.\n429: +* Without `\"interfaces\": {\"jumbo-frames\": true}` in the BNG Blaster configuration, frames larger than about 4 KB are not received completely.\n430: +\n431: +## Contact\n432: +\n433: +The kind is maintained by RtBrick, contact <bngblaster@rtbrick.com>.\n434: diff --git requirements**[^1] | :fontawesome-solid-microchip: 1 <br/>:fontawesome-solid-memory: 1 GB               |\n+| **Topology file**             | [bngblaster01.clab.yml][topofile]                                                  |\n+| **Name**                      | bngblaster01                                                                       |\n+\n+## Description\n+\n+A single BNG Blaster node with `eth1` connected to `eth2`. The A10NSP interface `eth1` emulates a PPPoE server and `eth2` the PPPoE clients, so the lab needs no device under test. Replace one side with a BNG to test it.\n+\n+The [startup-config](../manual/kinds/rtbrick_bngblaster.md#startup-configuration) `pppoe.json` establishes 10 PPPoE sessions with session traffic and traffic streams, and the test starts automatically once both links are attached. `run.json` enables the report with session and stream details and logging.\n+\n+## Use cases\n+\n+Follow the test while it is running:\n+\n+```bash\n+docker exec clab-bngblaster01-bngblaster \\\n+  bngblaster-cli /var/bngblaster/clab/run.sock session-counters\n+```\n+\n+or open the web UI at `http://clab-bngblaster01-bngblaster:8001`.\n+\n+When the lab is destroyed, the test is stopped and its report is written to `clab-bngblaster01/bngblaster/clab/run_report.json`.\n+\n+[topofile]: https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/tree/main/lab-examples/bngblaster01/bngblaster01.clab.yml\n+\n+[^1]: Resource requirements are provisional. Consult with the installation guides for additional information.\ndiff --git a/docs/lab-examples/bngblaster02.md b/docs/lab-examples/bngblaster02.md\nnew file mode 100644\nindex 0000000..f34c693\n--- /dev/null\n+++ b/docs/lab-examples/bngblaster02.md\n@@ -0,0 +1,46 @@\n+|                               |                                                                                    |\n+| ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n+| **Description**               | RtBrick BNG Blaster emulating an IS-IS topology towards FRR, verified with traffic |\n+| **Components**                | [RtBrick BNG Blaster](../manual/kinds/rtbrick_bngblaster.md), [FRR](../manual/kinds/frr.md) |\n+| **Resource requirements**[^1] | :fontawesome-solid-microchip: 1 <br/>:fontawesome-solid-memory: 1 GB               |\n+| **Topology file**             | [bngblaster02.clab.yml][topofile]                                                  |\n+| **Name**                      | bngblaster02                                                                       |\n+\n+## Description\n+\n+The BNG Blaster forms an IS-IS level 1 adjacency with FRR on `eth1` and advertises an emulated topology of 20 routers behind it, generated with [lspgen](https://rtbrick.github.io/bngblaster/routing/lspgen.html) and loaded from `isis.mrt`. FRR learns the routes to all emulated routers.\n+\n+Two traffic streams are sent from the second BNG Blaster interface `eth2` to the loopback addresses of the emulated routers `node1` (192.168.0.0) and `node20` (192.168.0.11). FRR routes them back to the BNG Blaster on `eth1`, which verifies the streams for loss. The packets sent before FRR installed the routes, usually within a few seconds after the start, are not received.\n+\n+```\n+bngblaster eth1 <---- IS-IS adjacency ----> eth1 frr\n+bngblaster eth2 ---- traffic streams -----> eth2 frr\n+```\n+\n+The test starts automatically once both links are attached.\n+\n+## Use cases\n+\n+The IS-IS database and routes of FRR:\n+\n+```bash\n+docker exec clab-bngblaster02-frr vtysh -c \"show isis database\"\n+docker exec clab-bngblaster02-frr vtysh -c \"show ip route isis\"\n+```\n+\n+The adjacency and the traffic streams on the BNG Blaster:\n+\n+```bash\n+docker exec clab-bngblaster02-bngblaster \\\n+  bngblaster-cli /var/bngblaster/clab/run.sock isis-adjacencies\n+docker exec clab-bngblaster02-bngblaster \\\n+  bngblaster-cli /var/bngblaster/clab/run.sock stream-summary\n+```\n+\n+When the lab is destroyed, the BNG Blaster is stopped first, withdraws its IS-IS topology and closes the adjacency before FRR and the links are removed, and the stream results are written to `clab-bngblaster02/bngblaster/clab/run_report.json`.\n+\n+FRR pads its IS-IS hellos to the interface MTU, which is 9500 for containerlab links by default, and sizes its CSNP and PSNP according to it as well. `isis.json` therefore enables `jumbo-frames`, sets the `mtu` of `eth1` to 9500 and raises the IS-IS `max-pdu-size` to 9497 (MTU minus 3 bytes for the LLC header). IS-IS PDUs larger than 1497 bytes are sent as LLC in Ethernet II frames with ethertype 0x8870, see [IS-IS jumbo frames](https://rtbrick.github.io/bngblaster/routing/isis.html#jumbo-frames). This requires BNG Blaster 1.2.0 or newer.\n+\n+[topofile]: https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/tree/main/lab-examples/bngblaster02/bngblaster02.clab.yml\n+\n+[^1]: Resource requirements are provisional. Consult with the installation guides for additional information.\ndiff --git a/docs/manual/kinds/index.md b/docs/manual/kinds/index.md\nindex f2ad825..b88310b 100644\n--- b/docs/manual/kinds/rtbrick_bngblaster.md\n@@ -0,0 +1,139 @@\n+---\n+search:\n+  boost: 4\n+kind_code_name: rtbrick_bngblaster\n+kind_display_name: RtBrick BNG Blaster\n+---\n+# -{{ kind_display_name }}-\n+\n+[-{{ kind_display_name }}-](https://github.com/rtbrick/bngblaster) is an open-source network tester for access and routing protocols. It emulates subscribers (PPPoE, IPoE, L2TP, IPTV) and routing protocols (IS-IS, OSPF, LDP, BGP including EVPN), and verifies millions of traffic streams. -{{ kind_display_name }}- node is identified with the `-{{ kind_code_name }}-` kind in the [topology file](../topo-def-file.md); `bngblaster` is accepted as a short alias.\n+\n+The container image runs the [BNG Blaster controller](https://github.com/rtbrick/bngblaster-controller), which manages the test instances and provides a REST API and web UI. Version 1.1.1 or newer of the controller is required, which is part of the image since BNG Blaster 1.1.0. The image `ghcr.io/rtbrick/bngblaster:1.2.0` or newer is recommended.\n+\n+## Getting -{{ kind_display_name }}- image\n+\n+The image is publicly available in the GitHub Container Registry as [`ghcr.io/rtbrick/bngblaster`](https://github.com/rtbrick/bngblaster/pkgs/container/bngblaster). It is used by default if the node has no `image` configured.\n+\n+```bash\n+docker pull ghcr.io/rtbrick/bngblaster:latest\n+```\n+\n+## Managing -{{ kind_display_name }}- nodes\n+\n+/// tab | Web UI and REST API\n+The controller serves a web UI and REST API on port 8001, from the lab host for example at `http://clab-<lab-name>-<node-name>:8001`. To reach it from a remote browser, publish the port with a different host port per node:\n+\n+```yaml\n+    bngblaster:\n+      kind: rtbrick_bngblaster\n+      ports:\n+        - 8001:8001\n+```\n+\n+///\n+\n+/// tab | CLI\n+`bngblaster-cli` sends commands to the control socket of the running test:\n+\n+```bash\n+docker exec -it clab-<lab-name>-<node-name> \\\n+  bngblaster-cli /var/bngblaster/clab/run.sock session-counters\n+```\n+\n+///\n+\n+/// tab | Shell\n+```bash\n+docker exec -it clab-<lab-name>-<node-name> bash\n+```\n+\n+///\n+\n+## Interface naming\n+\n+-{{ kind_display_name }}- uses the interface names of the links as they are, which are referenced in the BNG Blaster configuration:\n+\n+* `eth0` - management interface connected to the containerlab management network\n+* `eth1+` - data interfaces, any other name can be used as well\n+\n+## Features and options\n+\n+### Startup configuration\n+\n+With the [`startup-config`](../nodes.md#startup-config) property, a user sets the path to a BNG Blaster configuration file (JSON). It is copied to `/var/bngblaster/clab/config.json` in the container, and the controller starts this test instance (`clab`) automatically once all links of the node are attached.\n+\n+```yaml\n+topology:\n+  nodes:\n+    bngblaster:\n+      kind: rtbrick_bngblaster\n+      startup-config: pppoe.json\n+```\n+\n+Without a startup-config, or with [`suppress-startup-config`](../nodes.md#suppress-startup-config), only the controller is started, and tests are created and started through the web UI or REST API.\n+\n+As for other kinds, an existing `config.json` from a previous deployment is kept, so changes to the startup-config file take effect only after `containerlab destroy --cleanup`, with `containerlab deploy --reconfigure`, or with [`enforce-startup-config`](../nodes.md#enforce-startup-config) set for the node.\n+\n+The start arguments of the test, for example to write a report or log file, are read from `/var/bngblaster/clab/run.json` if present:\n+\n+```yaml\n+      binds:\n+        - run.json:/var/bngblaster/clab/run.json:ro\n+```\n+\n+```json\n+{\n+    \"report\": true,\n+    \"report_flags\": [\"sessions\", \"streams\"],\n+    \"logging\": true,\n+    \"logging_flags\": [\"info\", \"error\"]\n+}\n+```\n+\n+### Results\n+\n+The node's lab directory (`clab-<lab-name>/<node-name>`) is mounted as `/var/bngblaster`, the instance directory of the controller. The configuration, logs and the report of the test (`clab/run_report.json`) are kept there after the lab is destroyed, unless the lab directory is removed with `containerlab destroy --cleanup` or `containerlab deploy --reconfigure`.\n+\n+### Stopping the test\n+\n+The controller stops the test when the container is stopped, and BNG Blaster writes the report in all of the following cases:\n+\n+* `containerlab destroy`, with or without `--graceful`, and the removal of the node by `containerlab apply`: the node is stopped before any link or node of the lab is removed, also those of the device under test, so that BNG Blaster tears down its sessions gracefully (PPPoE: LCP Terminate-Request and PADT; routing sessions are closed). A teardown that takes longer than 30 seconds is ended at once, still with the report. For large tests, where the device under test should see every session closed, raise `BNGBLASTERCTRL_STOP_TIMEOUT` (e.g. `5m`) and the containerlab [`--timeout`](../../cmd/deploy.md#timeout) (default 2 minutes) to more than that plus 10 seconds, e.g. `containerlab destroy --timeout 6m`.\n+\n+* `containerlab stop`: the links are removed before the node is stopped, so the sessions can not be torn down gracefully. The controller detects the missing interfaces and stops the test at once.\n+* The test ends by itself or is stopped through the web UI, REST API or `bngblaster-cli`.\n+\n+`containerlab start` and `containerlab restart` start the test again once all links are attached. This removes the results of the previous run, so copy them before if needed.\n+\n+### Health check\n+\n+The node has a default health check, which is healthy while the test is running or after it finished without error, and unhealthy while waiting for the links, while the test starts, or if it failed. Other nodes can therefore wait for the test with [`wait-for`](../nodes.md#stages) and the `healthy` stage. The check is replaced by a [`healthcheck`](../nodes.md#healthcheck) configured for the node.\n+\n+### Environment variables\n+\n+The kind sets the following controller variables, which can be overridden with the node's `env`:\n+\n+| Variable                         | Description                                          | Default                            |\n+| -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |\n+| `BNGBLASTERCTRL_AUTOSTART`       | Instance started automatically                        | `clab` if a startup-config is set  |\n+| `BNGBLASTERCTRL_WAIT_INTERFACES` | Number of interfaces to wait for before the start     | number of links of the node        |\n+\n+All other controller options are available as `BNGBLASTERCTRL_<OPTION>` variables as well, for example `BNGBLASTERCTRL_STOP_TIMEOUT` (default `30s`) for the graceful teardown when the node is stopped, see the [controller documentation](https://github.com/rtbrick/bngblaster-controller).\n+\n+### IPv6\n+\n+The kind sets the sysctl `net.ipv6.conf.default.disable_ipv6=1`, so that the kernel does not use IPv6 on the data interfaces, which BNG Blaster handles itself. The management interface keeps IPv6. The sysctl is not set with `network-mode: host` or `network-mode: container:<name>`, where the node has no network namespace of its own.\n+\n+## Lab examples\n+\n+* [BNG Blaster PPPoE](../../lab-examples/bngblaster01.md) - PPPoE server and clients emulated back to back by one BNG Blaster node.\n+* [BNG Blaster and FRR IS-IS](../../lab-examples/bngblaster02.md) - emulated IS-IS topology advertised to FRR, verified with traffic streams through FRR.\n+\n+## Known issues and limitations\n+\n+* containerlab links have an MTU of 9500 by default, while BNG Blaster network interfaces use an MTU of 1500 by default and IS-IS accepts PDUs of up to 1497 bytes. Routers size IS-IS PDUs to the link MTU, for example padded hellos, and depending on the implementation LSPs and CSNPs, which are then rejected, so that the adjacency does not come up or the database is incomplete. Either configure `jumbo-frames`, the `mtu` of the interface and the IS-IS `max-pdu-size` of the BNG Blaster according to the link MTU, as in the [IS-IS lab example](../../lab-examples/bngblaster02.md) (requires BNG Blaster 1.2.0 or newer), or set the [`mtu`](../topo-def-file.md#links) of links to routing peers to 1500.\n+* Without `\"interfaces\": {\"jumbo-frames\": true}` in the BNG Blaster configuration, frames larger than about 4 KB are not received completely.\n+\n+## Contact\n+\n+The kind is maintained by RtBrick, contact <bngblaster@rtbrick.com>.\ndiff --git 46: // DefaultNode implements the Node interface and is embedded to the structs of all other nodes.
47: // It has common fields and methods that every node should typically have. Nodes can override
48: // methods if needed.
49: type DefaultNode struct {
50: 	Cfg              *clabtypes.NodeConfig
51: 	Mgmt             *clabtypes.MgmtNet
52: 	Runtime          clabruntime.ContainerRuntime
53: 	HostRequirements *clabtypes.HostRequirements
54: 	// SSHConfig is the SSH client configuration that a clab node requires.
55: 	SSHConfig *clabtypes.SSHConfig
56: 	// Indicates that the node should not start without no license file defined
57: 	LicensePolicy clabtypes.LicensePolicy
58: 	// OverwriteNode stores the interface used to overwrite methods defined
59: 	// for DefaultNode, so that particular nodes can provide custom implementations.
60: 	OverwriteNode NodeOverwrites
61: 	// List of link endpoints that are connected to the node.
62: 	Endpoints []clablinks.Endpoint
63: 	// Preserve topology endpoint objects while they belong to the parking node.
64: 	parkingNode *clablinks.ParkingNode
65: 	// Interface aliasing-related variables
66: 	InterfaceRegexp       *regexp.Regexp
67: 	InterfaceMappedPrefix string
68: 	InterfaceOffset       int
69: 	InterfaceHelp         string
70: 	FirstDataIfIndex      int
71: 	// State of the node
72: 	state      clabnodesstate.NodeState
73: 	statemutex sync.RWMutex
74: 	StopSignal clabtypes.Signal
75: }

77: // NewDefaultNode initializes the DefaultNode structure and receives a NodeOverwrites interface
78: // which is implemented by the node struct of a particular kind.
79: // This allows DefaultNode to access fields of the specific node struct in the methods defined for
80: // DefaultNode.
81: func NewDefaultNode(n NodeOverwrites) *DefaultNode {
82: 	dn := &DefaultNode{
83: 		HostRequirements: clabtypes.NewHostRequirements(),
84: 		OverwriteNode:    n,
85: 		LicensePolicy:    clabtypes.LicensePolicyNone,
86: 		SSHConfig:        clabtypes.NewSSHConfig(),
87: 	}
88: 
89: 	dn.InterfaceMappedPrefix = "eth"
90: 	dn.InterfaceOffset = 0
91: 	dn.FirstDataIfIndex = 0
92: 
93: 	return dn
94: }

96: func (d *DefaultNode) RequireMgmtReachable() error {
97: 	m := d.Runtime.Mgmt()
98: 	if m == nil || m.Driver != clabtypes.MgmtDriverMacvlan || m.MacvlanAuxEnabled() {
99: 		return nil
100: 	}
101: 
102: 	return fmt.Errorf(
103: 		"node %q post-deploy needs host-to-node management access, enable mgmt macvlan aux interface",
104: 		d.Cfg.ShortName,
105: 	)
106: }

120: 	if d.Cfg.IsRootNamespaceBased || d.Cfg.SkipUniquenessCheck {
121: 		return nil
122: 	}
123: 	_, err := d.LoadOrGenerateCertificate(ctx, params.Cert, params.TopologyName)

125: 		return fmt.Errorf("loading or generating certificate for node %q: %w", d.Cfg.ShortName, err)
126: 	}
127: 	return nil

171: func (d *DefaultNode) PullImage(ctx context.Context) error {
172: 	for imageKey, imageName := range d.OverwriteNode.GetImages(ctx) {
173: 		if imageName == "" {
174: 			return fmt.Errorf(
175: 				"missing required %q attribute for node %q",

178: 			)

181: 		if err != nil {

192: func (d *DefaultNode) Deploy(ctx context.Context, _ *DeployParams) error {
193: 	// Set the "CLAB_INTFS" variable to the number of interfaces (endpoints) a node has.
194: 	// This env var does not count in the eth0 interface that is automatically created by the
195: 	// container runtime. This env var is used by some containers (e.g. vrnetlab systems) to
196: 	// postpone the startup until all interfaces
197: 	// have been added to the container namespace.
198: 	d.Config().Env[clabconstants.ClabEnvIntfs] = strconv.Itoa(len(d.GetEndpoints()))
199: 
200: 	// create the container
201: 	cID, err := d.Runtime.CreateContainer(ctx, d.Cfg)
202: 	if err != nil {
203: 		return err
204: 	}
205: 
206: 	// start the container
207: 	_, err = d.Runtime.StartContainer(ctx, cID, d)
208: 	if err != nil {
209: 		return err
210: 	}
211: 
212: 	// Update the nodes state
213: 	d.SetState(clabnodesstate.Deployed)
214: 
215: 	return nil
216: }

218: // GetNSPath retrieves the nodes nspath.
219: func (d *DefaultNode) GetNSPath(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
220: 	var err error
221: 	nsp := ""
222: 
223: 	if d.Cfg.IsRootNamespaceBased {
224: 		netns, err := ns.GetCurrentNS()
225: 		if err != nil {
226: 			return "", err
227: 		}
228: 		nsp = netns.Path()
229: 	}
230: 	if nsp == "" {
231: 		nsp, err = d.Runtime.GetNSPath(ctx, d.OverwriteNode.GetContainerName())
232: 		if err != nil {
233: 			log.FromContext(ctx).Errorf(
234: 				"Unable to determine NetNS Path for node %s: %v",
235: 				d.Cfg.ShortName,
236: 				err,
237: 			)
238: 			return "", err
239: 		}
240: 	}
241: 
242: 	return nsp, err
243: }

247: 	return d.Cfg.IsRootNamespaceBased || d.Cfg.AutoRemove

250: // LinkApplyMode returns the conservative default for node kinds that do not
251: // explicitly opt into live hotplug or restart handling.
252: func (d *DefaultNode) LinkApplyMode(ctx context.Context) LinkApplyMode {
253: 	if d.Cfg != nil && (d.Cfg.IsRootNamespaceBased || d.Cfg.SkipUniquenessCheck) {
254: 		return LinkApplyModeLive
255: 	}
256: 	return d.ImageLinkApplyMode(ctx, LinkApplyModeRecreate)
257: }

259: // ImageLinkApplyMode allows node kinds to keep their normal fallback behavior
260: // while opting into live link apply when their image declares support for it.
261: func (d *DefaultNode) ImageLinkApplyMode(
262: 	ctx context.Context,
263: 	fallback LinkApplyMode,
264: ) LinkApplyMode {
265: 	if d.imageHasBoxenVendorLabel(ctx) {
266: 		return LinkApplyModeLive
267: 	}
268: 
269: 	return fallback
270: }

272: func (d *DefaultNode) imageHasBoxenVendorLabel(ctx context.Context) bool {
273: 	if d == nil || d.Cfg == nil || d.Cfg.Image == "" {
274: 		return false
275: 	}
276: 	if d.Runtime == nil {
277: 		log.FromContext(ctx).Debug("Skipping image label check for apply link hotplug support",
278: 			"image", d.Cfg.Image,
279: 			"reason", "node runtime is not initialized",
280: 		)
281: 		return false
282: 	}
283: 
284: 	inspect, err := d.Runtime.InspectImage(ctx, d.Cfg.Image)
285: 	if err != nil {
286: 		log.FromContext(ctx).Debug("Failed to inspect image for apply link hotplug support",
287: 			"image", d.Cfg.Image,
288: 			"error", err,
289: 		)
290: 		return false
291: 	}
292: 	if inspect == nil || inspect.Config.Labels == nil {
293: 		return false
294: 	}
295: 
296: 	return inspect.Config.Labels[boxenImageVendorLabel] == boxenImageVendorValue
297: }

299: func (d *DefaultNode) ComputeDiff(oldCfg, newCfg *clabtypes.NodeConfig) *clabtypes.TopologyDiff {
300: 	diff := &clabtypes.TopologyDiff{}
301: 
302: 	if oldCfg == nil || newCfg == nil {
303: 		return diff
304: 	}
305: 
306: 	if oldCfg.NodeType != newCfg.NodeType {
307: 		diff.Fields = append(diff.Fields, "Type")
308: 	}
309: 	if oldCfg.Kind != newCfg.Kind {
310: 		diff.Fields = append(diff.Fields, "Kind")
311: 	}
312: 	if oldCfg.Image != newCfg.Image {
313: 		diff.Fields = append(diff.Fields, "Image")
314: 	}
315: 	if oldCfg.GetHostname() != newCfg.GetHostname() {
316: 		diff.Fields = append(diff.Fields, "Hostname")
317: 	}
318: 	if oldCfg.Entrypoint != newCfg.Entrypoint {
319: 		diff.Fields = append(diff.Fields, "Entrypoint")
320: 	}
321: 	if oldCfg.Cmd != newCfg.Cmd {
322: 		diff.Fields = append(diff.Fields, "Cmd")
323: 	}
324: 	if !clabutils.SlicesEqualOrBothEmpty(oldCfg.Exec, newCfg.Exec) {
325: 		diff.Fields = append(diff.Fields, "Exec")
326: 	}
327: 	if !clabutils.MapsEqualOrBothEmpty(oldCfg.Env, newCfg.Env) {
328: 		diff.Fields = append(diff.Fields, "Env")
329: 	}
330: 	if !clabutils.SlicesEqualOrBothEmpty(oldCfg.Binds, newCfg.Binds) {
331: 		diff.Fields = append(diff.Fields, "Binds")
332: 	}
333: 	if !clabutils.SlicesEqualOrBothEmpty(oldCfg.Devices, newCfg.Devices) {
334: 		diff.Fields = append(diff.Fields, "Devices")
335: 	}
336: 	if !clabutils.SlicesEqualOrBothEmpty(oldCfg.CapAdd, newCfg.CapAdd) {
337: 		diff.Fields = append(diff.Fields, "CapAdd")
338: 	}
339: 	if oldCfg.Privileged != newCfg.Privileged {
340: 		diff.Fields = append(diff.Fields, "Privileged")
341: 	}
342: 	if oldCfg.CgroupnsMode != newCfg.CgroupnsMode {
343: 		diff.Fields = append(diff.Fields, "CgroupnsMode")
344: 	}
345: 	if oldCfg.CgroupParent != newCfg.CgroupParent {
346: 		diff.Fields = append(diff.Fields, "CgroupParent")
347: 	}
348: 	if oldCfg.PidMode != newCfg.PidMode {
349: 		diff.Fields = append(diff.Fields, "PidMode")
350: 	}
351: 	if !clabutils.MapsEqualOrBothEmpty(oldCfg.Tmpfs, newCfg.Tmpfs) {
352: 		diff.Fields = append(diff.Fields, "Tmpfs")
353: 	}
354: 	if !clabutils.SlicesEqualOrBothEmpty(oldCfg.SecurityOpts, newCfg.SecurityOpts) {
355: 		diff.Fields = append(diff.Fields, "SecurityOpts")
356: 	}
357: 	if oldCfg.ShmSize != newCfg.ShmSize {
358: 		diff.Fields = append(diff.Fields, "ShmSize")
359: 	}
360: 	if !clabutils.PortSetsEqual(oldCfg.PortSet, newCfg.PortSet) {
361: 		diff.Fields = append(diff.Fields, "Ports")
362: 	}
363: 	if oldCfg.User != newCfg.User {
364: 		diff.Fields = append(diff.Fields, "User")
365: 	}
366: 	if oldCfg.NetworkMode != newCfg.NetworkMode {
367: 		diff.Fields = append(diff.Fields, "NetworkMode")
368: 	}
369: 	if oldCfg.MgmtNet != newCfg.MgmtNet {
370: 		diff.Fields = append(diff.Fields, "MgmtNet")
371: 	}
372: 	if oldCfg.Runtime != newCfg.Runtime {
373: 		diff.Fields = append(diff.Fields, "Runtime")
374: 	}
375: 	if oldCfg.CPU != newCfg.CPU {
376: 		diff.Fields = append(diff.Fields, "CPU")
377: 	}
378: 	if oldCfg.CPUSet != newCfg.CPUSet {
379: 		diff.Fields = append(diff.Fields, "CPUSet")
380: 	}
381: 	if oldCfg.Memory != newCfg.Memory {
382: 		diff.Fields = append(diff.Fields, "Memory")
383: 	}
384: 	if oldCfg.License != newCfg.License {
385: 		diff.Fields = append(diff.Fields, "License")
386: 	}
387: 	_, oldInvalid := oldCfg.KindSpecificConfig.(InvalidKindSpecificConfig)
388: 	_, newInvalid := newCfg.KindSpecificConfig.(InvalidKindSpecificConfig)
389: 
390: 	if oldInvalid || newInvalid ||
391: 		!reflect.DeepEqual(oldCfg.KindSpecificConfig, newCfg.KindSpecificConfig) {
392: 		diff.Fields = append(diff.Fields, "KindSpecificConfig")
393: 	}
394: 
395: 	return diff
396: }
