WithTopoPath / WithLabNameOnly must run before WithNodeFilter so filterClabNodes\n\t// sees topology nodes (see filterClabNodes in clab.go).\n\tvarsFiles := opts.varsFiles\n\tif len(varsFiles) == 0 {\n\t\tvarsFiles = c.TopoPaths.VarsFilenamesAbsPath()\n\t}\n\n\tif clabutils.FileOrDirExists(topo) {\n\t\tnewOpts = append(newOpts, WithTopoPath(topo, varsFiles))\n\t} else {\n\t\t// Derive lab name from lab directory (format: clab-<labname>)\n\t\tlabName := filepath.Base(labDir)\n\t\tlabName = strings.TrimPrefix(labName, \"clab-\")\n\t\tlog.FromContext(ctx).Debugf(\n\t\t\t\"topology file %q not found, using lab name %q for destroy\",\n\t\t\ttopo,\n\t\t\tlabName,\n\t\t)\n\t\tnewOpts = append(newOpts, WithLabNameOnly(labName))\n\t}\n\n\tnewOpts = append(newOpts,\n\t\tWithNodeFilter(opts.nodeFilter),\n\t\t// during destroy we don't want to check bind paths\n\t\t// as it is irrelevant for this command.\n\t\tWithSkippedBindsPathsCheck(),\n\t\tWithRuntime(\n\t\t\tc.globalRuntimeName,\n\t\t\t&clabruntime.RuntimeConfig{\n\t\t\t\tDebug:            c.Config.Debug,\n\t\t\t\tTimeout:          c.timeout,\n\t\t\t\tGracefulShutdown: opts.graceful,\n\t\t\t},\n\t\t),\n\t)\n\n\tif opts.keepMgmtNet {\n\t\tnewOpts = append(newOpts, WithKeepMgmtNet())\n\t}\n\n\tcc, err := NewContainerLab(newOpts...)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\tif labDir != \"\" && clabutils.FileOrDirExists(labDir) {\n\t\t// adjust the labdir. Usually we take the PWD. but now on destroy time,\n\t\t// we might be in a different Dir.\n\t\terr = cc.TopoPaths.SetLabDir(labDir)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\t// populate the management network state (bridge names) destroy needs for the\n\t// removal of the iptables rules, without creating networks that are missing:\n\t// a lab deployed with a management network override leaves the topology's\n\t// default network uncreated, and creating it here would collide with the\n\t// subnets the override is using.\n\tif !cc.mgmtNetworksSkipped() {\n\t\tvar bridged clabtypes.MgmtNetworks\n\t\tfor _, m := range cc.allMgmtNetworks() {\n\t\t\tif m.Driver != clabtypes.MgmtDriverMacvlan {\n\t\t\t\tbridged = append(bridged, m)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\tif err = cc.resolveExistingMgmtNetworks(ctx, bridged); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\terr = cc.setMgmtNetLinkBridges()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\n\terr = cc.ResolveLinks()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\n\treturn cc, nil\n}\n\n// resolveExistingMgmtNetworks inspects the management networks that already exist\n// so their bridge names are populated, e.g. for the iptables cleanup on destroy.\n// Networks that do not exist are skipped: they hold no bridge yet, and the callers\n// must not create management networks. Runtimes that cannot check network existence\n// keep the create-or-inspect behavior.\nfunc (c *CLab) resolveExistingMgmtNetworks(\n\tctx context.Context,\n\tnetworks clabtypes.MgmtNetworks,\n) error {\n\tvar existing clabtypes.MgmtNetworks\n\n\tfor _, m := range networks {\n\t\trt, rtErr := c.mgmtRuntime(c.globalRuntimeName, m)\n\t\tif rtErr != nil {\n\t\t\t// runtimes without multiple network support never created extra networks\n\t\t\tlog.FromContext(ctx).Debug(\n\t\t\t\t\"Skipping management network resolution\", \"network\", m.Network, \"error\", rtErr,\n\t\t\t)\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tchecker, ok := rt.(clabruntime.MgmtNetworkChecker)\n\t\tif !ok {\n\t\t\texisting = append(existing, m)\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\n\t\texists, err := checker.MgmtNetworkExists(ctx)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\t\tif !exists {\n\t\t\tlog.FromContext(ctx).Debug(\n\t\t\t\t\"Skipping management network that does not exist\",\n\t\t\t\t\"network\",\n\t\t\t\tm.Network,\n\t\t\t)\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\n\t\texisting = append(existing, m)\n\t}\n\n\treturn c.createNetworks(ctx, existing)\n}\n\n// destroyLabDirs removes the lab directories of the destroyed labs. Directories\n// recorded in failedLabDirs are kept: their labs are still running, and the\n// directory holds the lab state a later destroy attempt relies on.\nfunc (c *CLab) destroyLabDirs(\n\tctx context.Context,\n\ttopos map[string]string,\n\tall bool,\n\tfailedLabDirs map[string]bool,\n) error {\n\tif len(topos) == 0 {\n\t\tlog.FromContext(ctx).Info(\"no containerlab containers found\")\n\n\t\tif !all {\n\t\t\tlabDir := c.TopoPaths.TopologyLabDir()\n\t\t\tif labDir == \"\" {\n\t\t\t\t// Try to infer the precise lab directory when TopologyLabDir is not set,\n\t\t\t\t// e.g. destroy --name without topology file. Only look for an exact\n\t\t\t\t// clab-<name> match, never a wildcard.\n\t\t\t\tif c.Config != nil && c.Config.Name != \"\" {\n\t\t\t\t\tcandidates := []string{}\n\t\t\t\t\tif base := os.Getenv(\"CLAB_LABDIR_BASE\"); base != \"\" {\n\t\t\t\t\t\tcandidates = append(candidates, filepath.Join(base, \"clab-\"+c.Config.Name))\n\t\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\t\tif c.TopoPaths.TopologyFileIsSet() {\n\t\t\t\t\t\tcandidates = append(\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\tcandidates,\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\tfilepath.Join(c.TopoPaths.TopologyFileDir(), \"clab-\"+c.Config.Name),\n\t\t\t\t\t\t)\n\t\t\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\t\t\tif wd, err := os.Getwd(); err == nil && wd != \"\" {\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\tcandidates = append(\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\tcandidates,\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\tfilepath.Join(wd, \"clab-\"+c.Config.Name),\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t)\n\t\t\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\t\tfor _, cand := range candidates {\n\t\t\t\t\t\tif _, err := os.Stat(cand); err == nil {\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\tlabDir = cand\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\tbreak\n\t\t\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\t\tif labDir == \"\" {\n\t\t\t\t\t\tlog.FromContext(ctx).Info(\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\"lab directory not found, nothing to clean\",\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\"candidates\",\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\tcandidates,\n\t\t\t\t\t\t)\n\t\t\t\t\t\treturn nil\n\t\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\t\tlog.FromContext(ctx).Info(\"lab directory not found, nothing to clean\")\n\t\t\t\t\treturn nil\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\t// Safety: only remove directories that look like a lab directory.\n\t\t\tbase := filepath.Base(labDir)\n\t\t\tif !strings.HasPrefix(base, \"clab-\") {\n\t\t\t\tlog.FromContext(ctx).Warnf(\n\t\t\t\t\t\"refusing to remove lab directory %q: unexpected name\",\n\t\t\t\t\tlabDir,\n\t\t\t\t)\n\t\t\t\treturn nil\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif c.Config != nil && c.Config.Name != \"\" {\n\t\t\t\texpected := \"clab-\" + c.Config.Name\n\t\t\t\tif base != expected {\n\t\t\t\t\tlog.FromContext(ctx).Warnf(\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\"refusing to remove lab directory %q: does not match expected %q\",\n\t\t\t\t\t\tlabDir,\n\t\t\t\t\t\texpected,\n\t\t\t\t\t)\n\t\t\t\t\treturn nil\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\tif _, err := os.Stat(labDir); os.IsNotExist(err) {\n\t\t\t\tlog.FromContext(ctx).Info(\n\t\t\t\t\t\"lab directory not found, nothing to clean\",\n\t\t\t\t\t\"path\",\n\t\t\t\t\tlabDir,\n\t\t\t\t)\n\t\t\t\treturn nil\n\t\t\t} else if err != nil {\n\t\t\t\tlog.FromContext(ctx).Debug(\n\t\t\t\t\t\"failed to stat lab directory, skipping\",\n\t\t\t\t\t\"path\",\n\t\t\t\t\tlabDir,\n\t\t\t\t\t\"error\",\n\t\t\t\t\terr,\n\t\t\t\t)\n\t\t\t\treturn nil\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\tlog.FromContext(ctx).Info(\"Removing lab directory\", \"path\", labDir)\n\t\t\tif err := os.RemoveAll(labDir); err != nil {\n\t\t\t\tlog.FromContext(ctx).Errorf(\"error deleting lab directory: %v\", err)\n\t\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\n\tfor _, labdir := range topos {\n\t\tif failedLabDirs[labdir] {\n\t\t\tlog.FromContext(ctx).Warnf(\n\t\t\t\t\"keeping lab directory %s: the lab was not destroyed, so its state is kept for a later attempt\",\n\t\t\t\tlabdir,\n\t\t\t)\n\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\n\t\terr := os.RemoveAll(labdir)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\tlog.FromContext(ctx).Errorf(\"error deleting lab directory: %v\", err)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\treturn nil\n}\n\nfunc (c *CLab) destroy(ctx context.Context, maxWorkers uint, keepMgmtNet bool) error {\n\tvar containers []clabruntime.GenericContainer\n\tvar orphanSidecars []clabruntime.GenericContainer\n\tvar err error\n\n\t// If we have nodes defined (from topology file), list containers by node.\n\t// Otherwise, list containers by lab name label (for destroy-by-name-only case).\n\tif len(c.Nodes) > 0 {\n\t\tcontainers, err = c.ListNodesContainersIgnoreNotFound(ctx)\n\t} else if c.Config.Name != \"\" {\n\t\tcontainers, err = c.ListContainers(ctx, WithListLabName(c.Config.Name))\n\t}\n\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\tif len(c.Nodes) == 0 {\n\t\tc.addMgmtNetworksFromContainers(containers)\n\t}\n\n\tif len(c.Nodes) > 0 {\n\t\ttailscaleContainers, err := c.discoverTailscaleContainers(ctx, c.nodeFilter)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\t\tfor _, ctr := range tailscaleContainers {\n\t\t\tif _, desired := c.Nodes[ctr.Labels[clabconstants.NodeName]]; desired {\n\t\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tcontainers = append(containers, ctr)\n\t\t\tif ctr.Labels[clabconstants.ToolType] == \"\" {\n\t\t\t\torphanSidecars = append(orphanSidecars, ctr)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tif len(containers) == 0 {\n\t\tif len(c.Nodes) > 0 && len(c.Links) > 0 {\n\t\t\tc.deleteSpecialLinkNodes(ctx)\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\n\tif maxWorkers == 0 {\n\t\tmaxWorkers = uint(len(containers))\n\t}\n\n\tlog.FromContext(ctx).Info(\"Destroying lab\", \"name\", c.Config.Name)\n\n\t// If we have nodes defined, use the normal node-based deletion.\n\t// Otherwise, delete containers directly via the runtime (for destroy-by-name-only case).\n\tif len(c.Nodes) > 0 {\n\t\tc.preDestroyNodes(ctx, slices.Collect(maps.Values(c.Nodes)), maxWorkers)\n\n\t\terr := clablinks.CleanupFilteredLinks(\n\t\t\tctx,\n\t\t\tc.Config.Topology.Links,\n\t\t\tc.Config.Name,\n\t\t\tc.nodeFilter,\n\t\t)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\t\tc.deleteNodes(ctx, maxWorkers)\n\t\tc.deleteContainersDirect(ctx, orphanSidecars)\n\t} else {\n\t\tc.deleteContainersDirect(ctx, containers)\n\t}\n\n\tc.deleteToolContainers(ctx)\n\n\tlog.FromContext(ctx).Info(\"Removing host entries\", \"path\", \"/etc/hosts\")\n\n\terr = c.DeleteEntriesFromHostsFile()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"error while trying to clean up the hosts file: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\n\tlog.FromContext(ctx).Info(\"Removing SSH config\", \"path\", c.TopoPaths.SSHConfigPath())\n\n\terr = c.RemoveSSHConfig(c.TopoPaths)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tlog.FromContext(ctx).Errorf(\"failed to remove ssh config file: %v\", err)\n\t}\n\n\t// delete container network namespaces symlinks\n\tfor _, node := range c.Nodes {\n\t\terr = node.DeleteNetnsSymlink(ctx)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"error while deleting netns symlinks: %w\", err)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\t// delete every defined management network, including extra networks\n\t// that apply may have left without nodes, and networks a previous\n\t// deployment recorded in the lab state but the topology no longer defines\n\tfor _, m := range c.mgmtNetworksForCleanup(ctx) {\n\t\tif m.Network == \"bridge\" || keepMgmtNet {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tlog.FromContext(ctx).Debugf(\"Calling DeleteNet method. Management network value is: %+v\", m)\n\n\t\trt, rtErr := c.mgmtRuntime(c.globalRuntimeName, m)\n\t\tif rtErr != nil {\n\t\t\t// runtimes without multiple network support never created extra networks\n\t\t\tlog.FromContext(ctx).Debug(\n\t\t\t\t\"Skipping management network deletion\",\n\t\t\t\t\"network\",\n\t\t\t\tm.Network,\n\t\t\t\t\"error\",\n\t\t\t\trtErr,\n\t\t\t)\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tif err = rt.DeleteNet(ctx); err != nil {\n\t\t\tswitch {\n\t\t\tcase err.Error() == fmt.Sprintf(\"Error: No such network: %s\", m.Network):\n\t\t\tcase strings.Contains(err.Error(), fmt.Sprintf(\" network %s not found\", m.Network)):\n\t\t\tdefault:\n\t\t\t\tlog.FromContext(ctx).Error(err)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\treturn nil\n}\n\nfunc (c *CLab) addMgmtNetworksFromContainers(containers []clabruntime.GenericContainer) {\n\tfor _, ctr := range containers {\n\t\tswitch name := ctr.NetworkName; name {\n\t\tcase \"\", \"unknown\", \"bridge\", \"host\", \"none\":\n\t\tdefault:\n\t\t\tif c.mgmtNetByNetwork(name).Network == name {\n\t\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tc.Config.MgmtNetworks = append(c.Config.MgmtNetworks, &clabtypes.MgmtNet{\n\t\t\t\tNetwork:        name,\n\t\t\t\tBridge:         ctr.Labels[clabconstants.NodeMgmtNetBr],\n\t\t\t\tExternalAccess: new(true),\n\t\t\t})\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\n// mgmtNetworksForCleanup returns the management networks to delete on destroy:\n// the topology-defined ones plus any network a previous deployment recorded in\n// the lab state but that the current topology no longer defines. Without the\n// state record a network dropped from the mgmt list would never be removed.\nfunc (c *CLab) mgmtNetworksForCleanup(ctx context.Context) clabtypes.MgmtNetworks {\n\tnetworks := c.allMgmtNetworks()\n\n\tstate, err := c.LoadState()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tlog.FromContext(ctx).Warn(\n\t\t\t\"Unable to load the management networks recorded in the lab state\",\n\t\t\t\"error\",\n\t\t\terr,\n\t\t)\n\t\treturn networks\n\t}\n\tif state == nil {\n\t\treturn networks\n\t}\n\n\tdefined := make(map[string]bool, len(networks))\n\tfor _, m := range networks {\n\t\tdefined[m.Network] = true\n\t}\n\tfor _, name := range state.MgmtNetworks {\n\t\tif defined[name] {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tdefined[name] = true\n\t\t// ExternalAccess mirrors the default every management network gets, so\n\t\t// the forwarding rule installed for the network is cleaned up too.\n\t\tnetworks = append(networks, &clabtypes.MgmtNet{\n\t\t\tNetwork:        name,\n\t\t\tExternalAccess: new(true),\n\t\t})\n\t}\n\n\treturn networks\n}\n\nfunc (c *CLab) deleteApplyNodes(ctx context.Context, plan *applyPlan) error {\n\tnodeNames := make([]string, 0, len(plan.deletedNodeSet)+len(plan.recreatedNodeSet))\n\tfor nodeName := range plan.deletedNodeSet {\n\t\tnodeNames = append(nodeNames, nodeName)\n\t}\n\tfor nodeName := range plan.recreatedNodeSet {\n\t\tnodeNames = append(nodeNames, nodeName)\n\t}\n\tsort.Strings(nodeNames)\n\n\thookNodes := make([]clabnodes.Node, 0, len(nodeNames))\n\tvar tailscaleContainers []clabruntime.GenericContainer\n\tfor _, nodeName := range nodeNames {\n\t\truntimeNode := plan.currentNodes[nodeName]\n\t\tif runtimeNode == nil {\n\t\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"runtime node %q not found\", nodeName)\n\t\t}\n\t\tif runtimeNode.external || runtimeNode.rootNamespaceBased {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tif len(runtimeNode.containers) > 0 &&\n\t\t\truntimeNode.containers[0].Labels[clabconstants.NodeKind] == clabnodestailscale.KindName {\n\t\t\ttailscaleContainers = append(tailscaleContainers, runtimeNode.containers...)\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tif node, ok := c.Nodes[nodeName]; ok {\n\t\t\thookNodes = append(hookNodes, node)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tvar logoutWg sync.WaitGroup\n\tfor _, ctr := range tailscaleContainers {\n\t\tlogoutWg.Go(func() { c.logoutTailscaleContainer(ctx, ctr) })\n\t}\n\tc.preDestroyNodes(ctx, hookNodes, 0)\n\tlogoutWg.Wait()\n\n\tfor _, nodeName := range nodeNames {\n\t\truntimeNode := plan.currentNodes[nodeName]\n\t\tif runtimeNode.external || runtimeNode.rootNamespaceBased {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tfor i := len(runtimeNode.containers) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {\n\t\t\tctr := runtimeNode.containers[i]\n\t\t\tif len(ctr.Names) == 0 {\n\t\t\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"runtime container for node %q has no name\", nodeName)\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\truntime := ctr.Runtime\n\t\t\tif runtime == nil {\n\t\t\t\truntime = c.globalRuntime()\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\taction := \"Deleting node\"\n\t\t\tif _, recreate := plan.recreatedNodeSet[nodeName]; recreate {\n\t\t\t\taction = \"Deleting node for recreate\"\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tlog.FromContext(ctx).Info(action, \"node\", nodeName, \"container\", ctr.Names[0])\n\t\t\tif err := runtime.DeleteContainer(ctx, ctr.Names[0]); err != nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"failed deleting node %q: %w\", nodeName, err)\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\t_ = clabutils.DeleteNetnsSymlink(ctx, ctr.Names[0])\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// preDestroyNodes runs the PreDestroy stage of the given nodes concurrently, before any of them\n// is deleted. Nodes without a container are skipped. A workers value of 0 runs all hooks at once.\nfunc (*CLab) preDestroyNodes(ctx context.Context, nodes []clabnodes.Node, workers uint) {\n\tif workers == 0 || workers > uint(len(nodes)) {\n\t\tworkers = uint(len(nodes))\n\t}\n\n\tsem := make(chan struct{}, workers)\n\twg := new(sync.WaitGroup)\n\n\tfor _, n := range nodes {\n\t\twg.Add(1)\n\t\tsem <- struct{}{}\n\n\t\tgo func() {\n\t\t\tdefer wg.Done()\n\t\t\tdefer func() { <-sem }()\n\n\t\t\tif n.GetContainerStatus(ctx) == clabruntime.NotFound {\n\t\t\t\treturn\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\tif err := n.PreDestroy(ctx); err != nil {\n\t\t\t\tlog.FromContext(ctx).Warnf(\n\t\t\t\t\t\"node %q pre-destroy hook failed: %v\",\n\t\t\t\t\tn.Config().ShortName,\n\t\t\t\t\terr,\n\t\t\t\t)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}()\n\t}\n\n\twg.Wait()\n}\n\nfunc (c *CLab) deleteNodes(ctx context.Context, workers uint) {\n\twg := new(sync.WaitGroup)\n\n\tconcurrentChan := make(chan clabnodes.Node)\n\n\tworkerFunc := func(i uint, input chan clabnodes.Node, wg *sync.WaitGroup) {\n\t\tdefer wg.Done()\n\n\t\tfor {\n\t\t\tselect {\n\t\t\tcase n := <-input:\n\t\t\t\tif n == nil {\n\t\t\t\t\tlog.FromContext(ctx).Debugf(\"Worker %d terminating...\", i)\n\t\t\t\t\treturn\n\t\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\t\terr := n.Delete(ctx)\n\t\t\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\t\t\tlog.FromContext(ctx).Errorf(\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\"could not remove container %q: %v\",\n\t\t\t\t\t\tn.Config().LongName,\n\t\t\t\t\t\terr,\n\t\t\t\t\t)\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tcase <-ctx.Done():\n\t\t\t\treturn\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\t// start concurrent workers\n\twg.Add(int(workers))\n\n\tfor i := range workers {\n\t\tgo workerFunc(i, concurrentChan, wg)\n\t}\n\n\t// send nodes to workers\n\tfor _, n := range c.Nodes {\n\t\tconcurrentChan <- n\n\t}\n\n\t// close channel to terminate the workers\n\tclose(concurrentChan)\n\n\twg.Wait()\n\n\t// Host and mgmt-br links must be removed only after node workers finish.\n\t// vxlan-stitch teardown deletes veth pairs from containers concurrently with\n\t// host-namespace VXLAN interfaces; running both at once races netlink deletes.\n\tc.deleteSpecialLinkNodes(ctx)\n}\n\nfunc (c *CLab) deleteSpecialLinkNodes(ctx context.Context) {\n\tspecialNodes := append(\n\t\t[]clablinks.Node{clablinks.GetHostLinkNode()},\n\t\tclablinks.GetMgmtBrLinkNodes()...,\n\t)\n\tfor _, n := range specialNodes {\n\t\terr := n.Delete(ctx)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\tlog.FromContext(ctx).Warn(err)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\n// deleteContainersDirect deletes containers directly via the runtime API.\n// This is used when we don't have node objects (e.g., destroy-by-name-only case).\nfunc (c *CLab) deleteContainersDirect(\n\tctx context.Context,\n\tcontainers []clabruntime.GenericContainer,\n) {\n\tfor _, cont := range containers {\n\t\tif len(cont.Names) == 0 {\n\t\t\tlog.FromContext(ctx).Warnf(\"skipping container %s with no names\", cont.ID)\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tname := cont.Names[0]\n\t\tlog.FromContext(ctx).Infof(\"Removing container: %s\", name)\n\n\t\tc.logoutTailscaleContainer(ctx, cont)\n\t\trt := cont.Runtime\n\t\tif rt == nil {\n\t\t\trt = c.globalRuntime()\n\t\t}\n\t\terr := rt.DeleteContainer(ctx, name)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\tlog.FromContext(ctx).Errorf(\"could not remove container %q: %v\", name, err)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc (c *CLab) deleteToolContainers(ctx context.Context) {\n\ttoolTypes := []string{\"sshx\", \"gotty\"}\n\n\tif len(c.nodeFilter) == 0 {\n\t\ttoolTypes = append(toolTypes, clabnodestailscale.ToolType)\n\t}\n\n\tfor _, toolType := range toolTypes {\n\t\ttoolFilter := []*clabtypes.GenericFilter{\n\t\t\t{\n\t\t\t\tFilterType: \"label\",\n\t\t\t\tField:      clabconstants.ToolType,\n\t\t\t\tOperator:   \"=\",\n\t\t\t\tMatch:      toolType,\n\t\t\t},\n\t\t\t{\n\t\t\t\tFilterType: \"label\",\n\t\t\t\tField:      clabconstants.Containerlab,\n\t\t\t\tOperator:   \"=\",\n\t\t\t\tMatch:      c.Config.Name,\n\t\t\t},\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tcontainers, err := c.globalRuntime().ListContainers(ctx, toolFilter)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\tlog.FromContext(ctx).Error(\n\t\t\t\t\"Failed to list tool containers\",\n\t\t\t\t\"tool\",\n\t\t\t\ttoolType,\n\t\t\t\t\"error\",\n\t\t\t\terr,\n\t\t\t)\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tif len(containers) == 0 {\n\t\t\tlog.FromContext(ctx).Debug(\n\t\t\t\t\"No tool containers found for lab\",\n\t\t\t\t\"tool\",\n\t\t\t\ttoolType,\n\t\t\t\t\"lab\",\n\t\t\t\tc.Config.Name,\n\t\t\t)\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tlog.FromContext(ctx).Info(\n\t\t\t\"Found tool containers associated with a lab\",\n\t\t\t\"tool\",\n\t\t\ttoolType,\n\t\t\t\"lab\",\n\t\t\tc.Config.Name,\n\t\t\t\"count\",\n\t\t\tlen(containers),\n\t\t)\n\n\t\tfor idx := range containers {\n\t\t\tcontainerName := container\",\n\t\t\t\t\"tool\",\n\t\t\t\ttoolType,\n\t\t\t\t\"container\",\n\t\t\t\tcontainerName,\n\t\t\t)\n\n\t\t\tc.logoutTailscaleContainer(ctx, containers[idx])\n\t\t\tif err := c.globalRuntime().DeleteContainer(ctx, containerName); err != nil {\n\t\t\t\tlog.FromContext(ctx).Error(\"Failed to remove tool container\", \"tool\", toolType,\n\t\t\t\t\t\"container\", Reasoning
The destroy flow: `preDestroyNodes` runs PreDestroy for all nodes before deletion; matches the doc claim.

Important: PreDestroy stops the container but does NOT park endpoints. Then `deleteNodes` calls `n.Delete(ctx)`, which removes endpoint links first and then deletes the container. Since the container is stopped, `e.GetLink().Remove(ctx)` — link removal for veth typically just deletes both veth ends; the container-side end is in a stopped container's netns... Actually stopping the container with runtime keeps the netns? Docker stop keeps the container and its netns. So link removal should still work.

But wait — an important subtlety in `DefaultNode.Delete`: it checks `d.OverwriteNode.GetContainerStatus(ctx) == NotFound` return nil. Since PreDestroy stopped it, status would be Stopped, not NotFound. Then `d.Runtime.DeleteContainer` removes it. Fine.

Now what about `n.StopSignal` — zero value? `clabtypes.Signal` is likely a string type. Let me check the type and the docker runtime's StopContainer handling of empty signal. In DefaultNode.Stop, it's used the same way (`d.StopSignal`), so this is the same pattern used by the default stop. Let me check `clabtypes.Signal` definition and how StopContainer handles it.

Also check `Node` interface (nodes/node.go) to confirm `Deploy`, `PreDestroy`, `Init` signatures.

5: package rtbrick_bngblaster

9: 	"fmt"
10: 	"os"
11: 	"path"

13: 	"strings"
14: 
15: 	clabconstants "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/constants"
16: 	clabnodes "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/nodes"

18: 	clabtypes "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/types"
19: 	clabutils "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/utils"
20: )
21: 
22: var kindNames = []string{"rtbrick_bngblaster", "bngblaster"}
23: 
24: const (
25: 	generateable     = true
26: 	generateIfFormat = "eth%d"
27: 
28: 	// DefaultImage is used if the node has no image configured.
29: 	DefaultImage = "ghcr.io/rtbrick/bngblaster:latest"
30: 
31: 	// instanceDir is the BNG Blaster controller config folder in the container,
32: 	// bound to the node's lab directory, so that the logs and reports of the
33: 	// test are kept in the lab directory.
34: 	instanceDir = "/var/bngblaster"
35: 	// instanceName is the controller instance started from the startup-config.
36: 	instanceName = "clab"
37: 	configFile   = "config.json"
38: 
39: 	envAutostart      = "BNGBLASTERCTRL_AUTOSTART"
40: 	envWaitInterfaces = "BNGBLASTERCTRL_WAIT_INTERFACES"
41: 
42: 	// sysctlDisableIPv6 disables IPv6 on the data interfaces, which containerlab
43: 	// attaches after the container started. Not net.ipv6.conf.all, which would
44: 	// also overwrite the default and disable IPv6 on the management interface.
45: 	sysctlDisableIPv6 = "net.ipv6.conf.default.disable_ipv6"
46: )
47: 
48: // defaultHealthcheck reports the node healthy while the test runs or after it
49: // finished without error. It is unhealthy while the controller waits for the
50: // links (up to 5 minutes by default), which the start period covers.
51: var defaultHealthcheck = clabtypes.HealthcheckConfig{
52: 	Test:        []string{"CMD", "/usr/bin/bngblasterctrl", "-health"},
53: 	Interval:    5,
54: 	Timeout:     3,
55: 	Retries:     3,
56: 	StartPeriod: 300,
57: }
58: 
59: // Register registers the node in the NodeRegistry.
60: func Register(r *clabnodes.NodeRegistry) {
61: 	generateNodeAttributes := clabnodes.NewGenerateNodeAttributes(generateable, generateIfFormat)
62: 	nrea := clabnodes.NewNodeRegistryEntryAttributes(nil, generateNodeAttributes, nil)
63: 
64: 	r.Register(kindNames, func() clabnodes.Node {
65: 		return new(bngblaster)
66: 	}, nrea)
67: }
68: 
69: type bngblaster struct {
70: 	clabnodes.DefaultNode
71: }
72: 
73: func (n *bngblaster) Init(cfg *clabtypes.NodeConfig, opts ...clabnodes.NodeOption) error {
74: 	n.DefaultNode = *clabnodes.NewDefaultNode(n)
75: 	n.Cfg = cfg
76: 
77: 	if n.Cfg.Image == "" {
78: 		n.Cfg.Image = DefaultImage
79: 	}
80: 
81: 	if n.Cfg.Env == nil {
82: 		n.Cfg.Env = map[string]string{}
83: 	}
84: 	if n.Cfg.StartupConfig != "" {
85: 		n.Cfg.ResStartupConfig = path.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, instanceName, configFile)
86: 		// A suppressed startup-config is not written, so there is no config
87: 		// to start the instance with.
88: 		if !n.Cfg.SuppressStartupConfig {
89: 			setDefault(n.Cfg.Env, envAutostart, instanceName)
90: 		}
91: 	}
92: 
93: 	// The node has no network namespace of its own with network-mode host or
94: 	// container:<name>, where the runtime rejects net.* sysctls.
95: 	if hasOwnNetns(n.Cfg.NetworkMode) {
96: 		if n.Cfg.Sysctls == nil {
97: 			n.Cfg.Sysctls = map[string]string{}
98: 		}
99: 		setDefault(n.Cfg.Sysctls, sysctlDisableIPv6, "1")
100: 	}
101: 
102: 	if n.Cfg.Healthcheck == nil {
103: 		hc := defaultHealthcheck
104: 		n.Cfg.Healthcheck = &hc
105: 	}
106: 
107: 	n.Cfg.Binds = append(n.Cfg.Binds, n.Cfg.LabDir+":"+instanceDir)
108: 
109: 	for _, o := range opts {
110: 		o(n)
111: 	}
112: 
113: 	return nil
114: }
115: 
116: func (n *bngblaster) PreDeploy(ctx context.Context, _ *clabnodes.PreDeployParams) error {
117: 	clabutils.CreateDirectory(n.Cfg.LabDir, clabconstants.PermissionsOpen)
118: 
119: 	if n.Cfg.StartupConfig == "" {
120: 		return nil
121: 	}
122: 
123: 	clabutils.CreateDirectory(path.Dir(n.Cfg.ResStartupConfig), clabconstants.PermissionsOpen)
124: 
125: 	cfg, err := os.ReadFile(n.Cfg.StartupConfig)
126: 	if err != nil {
127: 		return err
128: 	}
129: 
130: 	return n.GenerateConfig(ctx, n.Cfg.ResStartupConfig, string(cfg))
131: }
132: 
133: // Deploy lets the controller wait for all links before it starts the test.
134: func (n *bngblaster) Deploy(ctx context.Context, params *clabnodes.DeployParams) error {
135: 	if n.Cfg.Env[envAutostart] != "" {
136: 		setDefault(n.Cfg.Env, envWaitInterfaces, strconv.Itoa(len(n.GetEndpoints())))
137: 	}
138: 
139: 	return n.DefaultNode.Deploy(ctx, params)
140: }
141: 
142: // PreDestroy stops the container on destroy and apply. It runs before any link
143: // or node of the lab is removed, also those of the device under test, so that
144: // BNG Blaster can tear down its sessions over the links and write the report of
145: // the test. On SIGTERM the controller stops the test gracefully and ends the
146: // teardown at once after BNGBLASTERCTRL_STOP_TIMEOUT (default 30s), still with
147: // the report. The container is removed afterwards anyway, also if it did not
148: // stop, so a failed stop is not an error.
149: func (n *bngblaster) PreDestroy(ctx context.Context) error {
150: 	if n.GetContainerStatus(ctx) == clabruntime.Running {
151: 		_ = n.Runtime.StopContainer(ctx, n.GetContainerName(), n.StopSignal)
152: 	}
153: 
154: 	return nil
155: }
156: 
157: // CheckInterfaceName allows any interface name, except eth0 when the
158: // management interface uses it.
159: func (n *bngblaster) CheckInterfaceName() error {
160: 	nm := strings.ToLower(n.Cfg.NetworkMode)
161: 	for _, e := range n.Endpoints {
162: 		if e.GetIfaceName() == "eth0" && nm != "none" {
163: 			return fmt.Errorf(
164: 				"eth0 interface name is not allowed for %s node when network mode is not set to none",
165: 				n.Cfg.ShortName,
166: 			)
167: 		}
168: 	}
169: 
170: 	return n.CheckInterfaceOverlap()
171: }
172: 
173: // hasOwnNetns reports whether the node has a network namespace of its own.
174: func hasOwnNetns(networkMode string) bool {
175: 	nm := strings.ToLower(networkMode)
176: 
177: 	return nm != "host" && !strings.HasPrefix(nm, "container:")
178: }
179: 
180: func setDefault(m map[string]string, key, value string) {
181: 	if _, ok := m[key]; !ok {
182: 		m[key] = value
183: 	}
184: }

Reasoning
`StopContainer` with empty signal sends SIGTERM then waits `d.config.Timeout` seconds (default timeout — check the deploy default timeout: 2 minutes per docs). PreDestroy's stop blocks until the container stops or the timeout. The docs mention "raise ... the containerlab --timeout (default 2 minutes) to more than that plus 10 seconds" — consistent.

One issue: `PreDestroy` calls `n.Runtime.StopContainer(...)` directly rather than going through the Node's `Stop` — intentional, since `Stop` parks endpoints (which would remove links from the container netns; actually parking moves them out, but destroy would then remove links... they wanted the links to remain). Also `DefaultNode.Stop` would call PreStop, park endpoints, stop the container. The direct StopContainer skips parking. During destroy, links are removed by `CleanupFilteredLinks` and `Delete`. When the container is stopped but not removed, veth endpoints inside the container netns — link removal deletes the veth pair which is fine. OK.

Now, one potential correctness issue: `PreDestroy` also runs during `apply` (deleteApplyNodes calls preDestroyNodes). And what about `containerlab stop`? Stop calls `d.Stop` → PreStop (no-op) → ParkEndpoints → StopContainer. The docs say on `stop` the links are removed first — matches, since ParkEndpoints moves endpoints to parking netns. OK.

Another potential issue: `Deploy` override — `n.Cfg.Env[envAutostart] != ""`. If a user sets `env: {BNGBLASTERCTRL_AUTOSTART: "test"}`, then envWaitInterfaces gets set to the number of endpoints (default). Fine.

But there's a subtle bug: `Deploy` runs `setDefault(env, envWaitInterfaces, count)` where count = len(n.GetEndpoints()). If the node has no links (0 endpoints), sets "0". The controller would wait for 0 interfaces and start immediately. Fine.

Now, what about `generateable = true` and `generateIfFormat = "eth%d"`? This affects `containerlab generate` support. Check NewGenerateNodeAttributes — fine.

Next: check that `n.Cfg.Binds = append(n.Cfg.Binds, n.Cfg.LabDir+":"+instanceDir)` — docker bind format needs absolute path on host. LabDir is absolute. OK. But — check `binds` validation: in core config, binds are validated (WithSkippedBindsPathsCheck during destroy). Bind path check: `clabutils.ResolvePath`? Let me check bind path validation which may reject a directory bind that doesn't exist? Actually PreDeploy creates the LabDir before... wait, ordering: bind path validation happens at topology load time (checkBindsPaths?), which may check that the source path of each bind exists. Let me check.

Also, other kinds bind LabDir too? e.g. srl binds labdir? Let me grep for `Binds = append` patterns in other nodes.

The bngblaster PreDeploy doesn't call it, so user-specified `certificate` for the node is silently ignored. But is that a practical scenario for a traffic generator? It's a minor regression risk. The `certificate` key is a per-node option in the schema, applicable to all kinds. If a bngblaster user sets it, silently nothing happens. 199:

201: 	// bundled template otherwise. Routing it through GenerateConfig is what
202: 	// makes enforce-startup-config, suppress-startup-config and templating
203: 	// behave the same way here as for every other kind.
204: 	cfgTemplate := defaultCfgTemplate

216:

218: 	if err != nil {
219: 		return fmt.Errorf("node=%s, failed to generate config: %w", nodeCfg.ShortName, err)
220: 	}

Reasoning
So comparable kinds (frr) do call `LoadOrGenerateCertificate` in their PreDeploy. The bngblaster PreDeploy skips cert loading. If a user sets `certificate:` on a bngblaster node, nothing happens (silently). This mirrors frr which handles it. Is this worth a finding? It's a P4/P3 — the node-level `certificate` option is documented generically (docs/manual/nodes.md?) — I'd need to check whether the certificate option is documented as kind-agnostic. Since `DefaultNode.PreDeploy` runs it for kinds that don't override PreDeploy, kinds overriding must call it themselves (like frr does). So bngblaster silently drops the generic `certificate` node option. I'll note it as P4 (edge case, low practical use for a traffic generator) or P3? The impact: user sets `certificate: clab-cert` expecting CA-signed cert; gets default behavior (or maybe breaks the controller if it expects certs? The controller is bngblasterctrl — doesn't use TLS certs from containerlab). P4 seems right... Actually wait — silently ignoring a documented per-node option is a real correctness gap for users. But for this kind, no in-container consumer of containerlab certs exists. I'll make it P4.

Also SSHPubKeys — only used by frr-like kinds. Not relevant.

699: +// Copyright 2026 RtBrick, Inc.
700: +// Licensed under the BSD 3-Clause License.

702: +
703: +package rtbrick_bngblaster
704: +
705: +import (
706: +	"context"
707: +	"fmt"
708: +	"os"
709: +	"path"
710: +	"strconv"
711: +	"strings"
712: +
713: +	clabconstants "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/constants"
714: +	clabnodes "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/nodes"
715: +	clabruntime "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/runtime"
716: +	clabtypes "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/types"
717: +	clabutils "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/utils"
718: +)
719: +
720: +var kindNames = []string{"rtbrick_bngblaster", "bngblaster"}
721: +
722: +const (
723: +	generateable     = true
724: +	generateIfFormat = "eth%d"
725: +
726: +	// DefaultImage is used if the node has no image configured.
727: +	DefaultImage = "ghcr.io/rtbrick/bngblaster:latest"
728: +
729: +	// instanceDir is the BNG Blaster controller config folder in the container,
730: +	// bound to the node's lab directory, so that the logs and reports of the
731: +	// test are kept in the lab directory.
732: +	instanceDir = "/var/bngblaster"
733: +	// instanceName is the controller instance started from the startup-config.
734: +	instanceName = "clab"
735: +	configFile   = "config.json"
736: +
737: +	envAutostart      = "BNGBLASTERCTRL_AUTOSTART"
738: +	envWaitInterfaces = "BNGBLASTERCTRL_WAIT_INTERFACES"
739: +
740: +	// sysctlDisableIPv6 disables IPv6 on the data interfaces, which containerlab
741: +	// attaches after the container started. Not net.ipv6.conf.all, which would
742: +	// also overwrite the default and disable IPv6 on the management interface.
743: +	sysctlDisableIPv6 = "net.ipv6.conf.default.disable_ipv6"
744: +)
745: +
746: +// defaultHealthcheck reports the node healthy while the test runs or after it
747: +// finished without error. It is unhealthy while the controller waits for the
748: +// links (up to 5 minutes by default), which the start period covers.
749: +var defaultHealthcheck = clabtypes.HealthcheckConfig{
750: +	Test:        []string{"CMD", "/usr/bin/bngblasterctrl", "-health"},
751: +	Interval:    5,
752: +	Timeout:     3,
753: +	Retries:     3,
754: +	StartPeriod: 300,
755: +}
756: +
757: +// Register registers the node in the NodeRegistry.
758: +func Register(r *clabnodes.NodeRegistry) {
759: +	generateNodeAttributes := clabnodes.NewGenerateNodeAttributes(generateable, generateIfFormat)
760: +	nrea := clabnodes.NewNodeRegistryEntryAttributes(nil, generateNodeAttributes, nil)
761: +
762: +	r.Register(kindNames, func() clabnodes.Node {
763: +		return new(bngblaster)
764: +	}, nrea)
765: +}
766: +
767: +type bngblaster struct {
768: +	clabnodes.DefaultNode
769: +}
770: +
771: +func (n *bngblaster) Init(cfg *clabtypes.NodeConfig, opts ...clabnodes.NodeOption) error {
772: +	n.DefaultNode = *clabnodes.NewDefaultNode(n)
773: +	n.Cfg = cfg
774: +
775: +	if n.Cfg.Image == "" {
776: +		n.Cfg.Image = DefaultImage
777: +	}
778: +
779: +	if n.Cfg.Env == nil {
780: +		n.Cfg.Env = map[string]string{}
781: +	}
782: +	if n.Cfg.StartupConfig != "" {
783: +		n.Cfg.ResStartupConfig = path.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, instanceName, configFile)
784: +		// A suppressed startup-config is not written, so there is no config
785: +		// to start the instance with.
786: +		if !n.Cfg.SuppressStartupConfig {
787: +			setDefault(n.Cfg.Env, envAutostart, instanceName)
788: +		}
789: +	}
790: +
791: +	// The node has no network namespace of its own with network-mode host or
792: +	// container:<name>, where the runtime rejects net.* sysctls.
793: +	if hasOwnNetns(n.Cfg.NetworkMode) {
794: +		if n.Cfg.Sysctls == nil {
795: +			n.Cfg.Sysctls = map[string]string{}
796: +		}
797: +		setDefault(n.Cfg.Sysctls, sysctlDisableIPv6, "1")
798: +	}
799: +
800: +	if n.Cfg.Healthcheck == nil {
801: +		hc := defaultHealthcheck
802: +		n.Cfg.Healthcheck = &hc
803: +	}
804: +
805: +	n.Cfg.Binds = append(n.Cfg.Binds, n.Cfg.LabDir+":"+instanceDir)
806: +
807: +	for _, o := range opts {
808: +		o(n)
809: +	}
810: +
811: +	return nil
812: +}
813: +
814: +func (n *bngblaster) PreDeploy(ctx context.Context, _ *clabnodes.PreDeployParams) error {
815: +	clabutils.CreateDirectory(n.Cfg.LabDir, clabconstants.PermissionsOpen)
816: +
817: +	if n.Cfg.StartupConfig == "" {
818: +		return nil
819: +	}
820: +
821: +	clabutils.CreateDirectory(path.Dir(n.Cfg.ResStartupConfig), clabconstants.PermissionsOpen)
822: +
823: +	cfg, err := os.ReadFile(n.Cfg.StartupConfig)
824: +	if err != nil {
825: +		return err
826: +	}
827: +
828: +	return n.GenerateConfig(ctx, n.Cfg.ResStartupConfig, string(cfg))
829: +}
830: +
831: +// Deploy lets the controller wait for all links before it starts the test.
832: +func (n *bngblaster) Deploy(ctx context.Context, params *clabnodes.DeployParams) error {
833: +	if n.Cfg.Env[envAutostart] != "" {
834: +		setDefault(n.Cfg.Env, envWaitInterfaces, strconv.Itoa(len(n.GetEndpoints())))
835: +	}
836: +
837: +	return n.DefaultNode.Deploy(ctx, params)
838: +}
839: +
840: +// PreDestroy stops the container on destroy and apply. It runs before any link
841: +// or node of the lab is removed, also those of the device under test, so that
842: +// BNG Blaster can tear down its sessions over the links and write the report of
843: +// the test. On SIGTERM the controller stops the test gracefully and ends the
844: +// teardown at once after BNGBLASTERCTRL_STOP_TIMEOUT (default 30s), still with
845: +// the report. The container is removed afterwards anyway, also if it did not
846: +// stop, so a failed stop is not an error.
847: +func (n *bngblaster) PreDestroy(ctx context.Context) error {
848: +	if n.GetContainerStatus(ctx) == clabruntime.Running {
849: +		_ = n.Runtime.StopContainer(ctx, n.GetContainerName(), n.StopSignal)
850: +	}
851: +
852: +	return nil
853: +}
854: +
855: +// CheckInterfaceName allows any interface name, except eth0 when the
856: +// management interface uses it.
857: +func (n *bngblaster) CheckInterfaceName() error {
858: +	nm := strings.ToLower(n.Cfg.NetworkMode)
859: +	for _, e := range n.Endpoints {
860: +		if e.GetIfaceName() == "eth0" && nm != "none" {
861: +			return fmt.Errorf(
862: +				"eth0 interface name is not allowed for %s node when network mode is not set to none",
863: +				n.Cfg.ShortName,
864: +			)
865: +		}
866: +	}
867: +
868: +	return n.CheckInterfaceOverlap()
869: +}
870: +
871: +// hasOwnNetns reports whether the node has a network namespace of its own.
872: +func hasOwnNetns(networkMode string) bool {
873: +	nm := strings.ToLower(networkMode)
874: +
875: +	return nm != "host" && !strings.HasPrefix(nm, "container:")
876: +}
877: +
878: +func setDefault(m map[string]string, key, value string) {
879: +	if _, ok := m[key]; !ok {
880: +		m[key] = value
881: +	}
882: +}

Reasoning
The `topology.kinds` section also has per-kind entries. Question: does the schema's `topology.kinds` section contain an entry for every kind? The test topology file `tests/17-rtbrick-bngblaster/01-bngblaster.clab.yml` uses `topology.kinds.rtbrick_bngblaster` with `image` and `binds`. If the schema's kinds section doesn't include `rtbrick_bngblaster`, does it have `additionalProperties: false` at the end? If so, that topology file would fail schema validation (though I don't think containerlab validates the schema at deploy time by default — the schema is for editors/`clab validate`?). Let me check the end of the kinds section for additionalProperties, and whether kinds like `veesix_osvbng` or `ostinato` have entries under `topology.kinds`. The grep earlier for `veesix_osvbng` only found lines 290, 3994 — NOT under the kinds section. So existing added kinds (veesix_osvbng, spirent_stc) do NOT have entries under `topology.kinds` either. So the convention is: only some kinds have entries there. Check if `additionalProperties` is set on the kinds object.

197: +| **Name**                      | bngblaster01                                                                       |
198: +
199: +## Description
200: +
201: +A single BNG Blaster node with `eth1` connected to `eth2`. The A10NSP interface `eth1` emulates a PPPoE server and `eth2` the PPPoE clients, so the lab needs no device under test. Replace one side with a BNG to test it.
202: +
203: +The [startup-config](../manual/kinds/rtbrick_bngblaster.md#startup-configuration) `pppoe.json` establishes 10 PPPoE sessions with session traffic and traffic streams, and the test starts automatically once both links are attached. `run.json` enables the report with session and stream details and logging.
204: +
205: +## Use cases
206: +
207: +Follow the test while it is running:
208: +
209: +```bash
210: +docker exec clab-bngblaster01-bngblaster \
211: +  bngblaster-cli /var/bngblaster/clab/run.sock session-counters
212: +```
213: +
214: +or open the web UI at `http://clab-bngblaster01-bngblaster:8001`.
215: +
216: +When the lab is destroyed, the test is stopped and its report is written to `clab-bngblaster01/bngblaster/clab/run_report.json`.
217: +
218: +[topofile]: https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/tree/main/lab-examples/bngblaster01/bngblaster01.clab.yml
219: +
220: +[^1]: Resource requirements are provisional. Consult with the installation guides for additional information.

222: new file mode 100644
223: index 0000000..f34c693
224: --- /dev/null
225: +++ b/docs/lab-examples/bngblaster02.md
226: @@ -0,0 +1,46 @@
227: +|                               |                                                                                    |
228: +| ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
229: +| **Description**               | RtBrick BNG Blaster emulating an IS-IS topology towards FRR, verified with traffic |
230: +| **Components**                | [RtBrick BNG Blaster](../manual/kinds/rtbrick_bngblaster.md), [FRR](../manual/kinds/frr.md) |
231: +| **Resource requirements**[^1] | :fontawesome-solid-microchip: 1 <br/>:fontawesome-solid-memory: 1 GB               |
232: +| **Topology file**             | [bngblaster02.clab.yml][topofile]                                                  |
233: +| **Name**                      | bngblaster02                                                                       |
234: +
235: +## Description
236: +
237: +The BNG Blaster forms an IS-IS level 1 adjacency with FRR on `eth1` and advertises an emulated topology of 20 routers behind it, generated with [lspgen](https://rtbrick.github.io/bngblaster/routing/lspgen.html) and loaded from `isis.mrt`. FRR learns the routes to all emulated routers.
238: +
239: +Two traffic streams are sent from the second BNG Blaster interface `eth2` to the loopback addresses of the emulated routers `node1` (192.168.0.0) and `node20` (192.168.0.11). FRR routes them back to the BNG Blaster on `eth1`, which verifies the streams for loss. The packets sent before FRR installed the routes, usually within a few seconds after the start, are not received.
240: +
241: +```
242: +bngblaster eth1 <---- IS-IS adjacency ----> eth1 frr
243: +bngblaster eth2 ---- traffic streams -----> eth2 frr
244: +```
245: +
246: +The test starts automatically once both links are attached.
247: +
248: +## Use cases
249: +
250: +The IS-IS database and routes of FRR:
251: +
252: +```bash
253: +docker exec clab-bngblaster02-frr vtysh -c "show isis database"
254: +docker exec clab-bngblaster02-frr vtysh -c "show ip route isis"
255: +```
256: +
257: +The adjacency and the traffic streams on the BNG Blaster:
258: +
259: +```bash
260: +docker exec clab-bngblaster02-bngblaster \
261: +  bngblaster-cli /var/bngblaster/clab/run.sock isis-adjacencies
262: +docker exec clab-bngblaster02-bngblaster \
263: +  bngblaster-cli /var/bngblaster/clab/run.sock stream-summary
264: +```
265: +
266: +When the lab is destroyed, the BNG Blaster is stopped first, withdraws its IS-IS topology and closes the adjacency before FRR and the links are removed, and the stream results are written to `clab-bngblaster02/bngblaster/clab/run_report.json`.
267: +
268: +FRR pads its IS-IS hellos to the interface MTU, which is 9500 for containerlab links by default, and sizes its CSNP and PSNP according to it as well. `isis.json` therefore enables `jumbo-frames`, sets the `mtu` of `eth1` to 9500 and raises the IS-IS `max-pdu-size` to 9497 (MTU minus 3 bytes for the LLC header). IS-IS PDUs larger than 1497 bytes are sent as LLC in Ethernet II frames with ethertype 0x8870, see [IS-IS jumbo frames](https://rtbrick.github.io/bngblaster/routing/isis.html#jumbo-frames). This requires BNG Blaster 1.2.0 or newer.
269: +
270: +[topofile]: https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/tree/main/lab-examples/bngblaster02/bngblaster02.clab.yml
271: +
272: +[^1]: Resource requirements are provisional. Consult with the installation guides for additional information.

289: diff --git a/docs/manual/kinds/rtbrick_bngblaster.md b/docs/manual/kinds/rtbrick_bngblaster.md
290: new file mode 100644
291: index 0000000..6e19cc2
292: --- /dev/null
293: +++ b/docs/manual/kinds/rtbrick_bngblaster.md
294: @@ -0,0 +1,139 @@
295: +---
296: +search:
297: +  boost: 4
298: +kind_code_name: rtbrick_bngblaster
299: +kind_display_name: RtBrick BNG Blaster
300: +---
301: +# -{{ kind_display_name }}-
302: +
303: +[-{{ kind_display_name }}-](https://github.com/rtbrick/bngblaster) is an open-source network tester for access and routing protocols. It emulates subscribers (PPPoE, IPoE, L2TP, IPTV) and routing protocols (IS-IS, OSPF, LDP, BGP including EVPN), and verifies millions of traffic streams. -{{ kind_display_name }}- node is identified with the `-{{ kind_code_name }}-` kind in the [topology file](../topo-def-file.md); `bngblaster` is accepted as a short alias.
304: +
305: +The container image runs the [BNG Blaster controller](https://github.com/rtbrick/bngblaster-controller), which manages the test instances and provides a REST API and web UI. Version 1.1.1 or newer of the controller is required, which is part of the image since BNG Blaster 1.1.0. The image `ghcr.io/rtbrick/bngblaster:1.2.0` or newer is recommended.
306: +
307: +## Getting -{{ kind_display_name }}- image
308: +
309: +The image is publicly available in the GitHub Container Registry as [`ghcr.io/rtbrick/bngblaster`](https://github.com/rtbrick/bngblaster/pkgs/container/bngblaster). It is used by default if the node has no `image` configured.
310: +
311: +```bash
312: +docker pull ghcr.io/rtbrick/bngblaster:latest
313: +```
314: +
315: +## Managing -{{ kind_display_name }}- nodes
316: +
317: +/// tab | Web UI and REST API
318: +The controller serves a web UI and REST API on port 8001, from the lab host for example at `http://clab-<lab-name>-<node-name>:8001`. To reach it from a remote browser, publish the port with a different host port per node:
319: +
320: +```yaml
321: +    bngblaster:
322: +      kind: rtbrick_bngblaster
323: +      ports:
324: +        - 8001:8001
325: +```
326: +
327: +///
328: +
329: +/// tab | CLI
330: +`bngblaster-cli` sends commands to the control socket of the running test:
331: +
332: +```bash
333: +docker exec -it clab-<lab-name>-<node-name> \
334: +  bngblaster-cli /var/bngblaster/clab/run.sock session-counters
335: +```
336: +
337: +///
338: +
339: +/// tab | Shell
340: +```bash
341: +docker exec -it clab-<lab-name>-<node-name> bash
342: +```
343: +
344: +///
345: +
346: +## Interface naming
347: +
348: +-{{ kind_display_name }}- uses the interface names of the links as they are, which are referenced in the BNG Blaster configuration:
349: +
350: +* `eth0` - management interface connected to the containerlab management network
351: +* `eth1+` - data interfaces, any other name can be used as well
352: +
353: +## Features and options
354: +
355: +### Startup configuration
356: +
357: +With the [`startup-config`](../nodes.md#startup-config) property, a user sets the path to a BNG Blaster configuration file (JSON). It is copied to `/var/bngblaster/clab/config.json` in the container, and the controller starts this test instance (`clab`) automatically once all links of the node are attached.
358: +
359: +```yaml
360: +topology:
361: +  nodes:
362: +    bngblaster:
363: +      kind: rtbrick_bngblaster
364: +      startup-config: pppoe.json
365: +```
366: +
367: +Without a startup-config, or with [`suppress-startup-config`](../nodes.md#suppress-startup-config), only the controller is started, and tests are created and started through the web UI or REST API.
368: +
369: +As for other kinds, an existing `config.json` from a previous deployment is kept, so changes to the startup-config file take effect only after `containerlab destroy --cleanup`, with `containerlab deploy --reconfigure`, or with [`enforce-startup-config`](../nodes.md#enforce-startup-config) set for the node.
370: +
371: +The start arguments of the test, for example to write a report or log file, are read from `/var/bngblaster/clab/run.json` if present:
372: +
373: +```yaml
374: +      binds:
375: +        - run.json:/var/bngblaster/clab/run.json:ro
376: +```
377: +
378: +```json
379: +{
380: +    "report": true,
381: +    "report_flags": ["sessions", "streams"],
382: +    "logging": true,
383: +    "logging_flags": ["info", "error"]
384: +}
385: +```
386: +
387: +### Results
388: +
389: +The node's lab directory (`clab-<lab-name>/<node-name>`) is mounted as `/var/bngblaster`, the instance directory of the controller. The configuration, logs and the report of the test (`clab/run_report.json`) are kept there after the lab is destroyed, unless the lab directory is removed with `containerlab destroy --cleanup` or `containerlab deploy --reconfigure`.
390: +
391: +### Stopping the test
392: +
393: +The controller stops the test when the container is stopped, and BNG Blaster writes the report in all of the following cases:
394: +
395: +* `containerlab destroy`, with or without `--graceful`, and the removal of the node by `containerlab apply`: the node is stopped before any link or node of the lab is removed, also those of the device under test, so that BNG Blaster tears down its sessions gracefully (PPPoE: LCP Terminate-Request and PADT; routing sessions are closed). A teardown that takes longer than 30 seconds is ended at once, still with the report. For large tests, where the device under test should see every session closed, raise `BNGBLASTERCTRL_STOP_TIMEOUT` (e.g. `5m`) and the containerlab [`--timeout`](../../cmd/deploy.md#timeout) (default 2 minutes) to more than that plus 10 seconds, e.g. `containerlab destroy --timeout 6m`.
396: +
397: +* `containerlab stop`: the links are removed before the node is stopped, so the sessions can not be torn down gracefully. The controller detects the missing interfaces and stops the test at once.
398: +* The test ends by itself or is stopped through the web UI, REST API or `bngblaster-cli`.
399: +
400: +`containerlab start` and `containerlab restart` start the test again once all links are attached. This removes the results of the previous run, so copy them before if needed.
401: +
402: +### Health check
403: +
404: +The node has a default health check, which is healthy while the test is running or after it finished without error, and unhealthy while waiting for the links, while the test starts, or if it failed. Other nodes can therefore wait for the test with [`wait-for`](../nodes.md#stages) and the `healthy` stage. The check is replaced by a [`healthcheck`](../nodes.md#healthcheck) configured for the node.
405: +
406: +### Environment variables
407: +
408: +The kind sets the following controller variables, which can be overridden with the node's `env`:
409: +
410: +| Variable                         | Description                                          | Default                            |
411: +| -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
412: +| `BNGBLASTERCTRL_AUTOSTART`       | Instance started automatically                        | `clab` if a startup-config is set  |
413: +| `BNGBLASTERCTRL_WAIT_INTERFACES` | Number of interfaces to wait for before the start     | number of links of the node        |
414: +
415: +All other controller options are available as `BNGBLASTERCTRL_<OPTION>` variables as well, for example `BNGBLASTERCTRL_STOP_TIMEOUT` (default `30s`) for the graceful teardown when the node is stopped, see the [controller documentation](https://github.com/rtbrick/bngblaster-controller).
416: +
417: +### IPv6
418: +
419: +The kind sets the sysctl `net.ipv6.conf.default.disable_ipv6=1`, so that the kernel does not use IPv6 on the data interfaces, which BNG Blaster handles itself. The management interface keeps IPv6. The sysctl is not set with `network-mode: host` or `network-mode: container:<name>`, where the node has no network namespace of its own.
420: +
421: +## Lab examples
422: +
423: +* [BNG Blaster PPPoE](../../lab-examples/bngblaster01.md) - PPPoE server and clients emulated back to back by one BNG Blaster node.
424: +* [BNG Blaster and FRR IS-IS](../../lab-examples/bngblaster02.md) - emulated IS-IS topology advertised to FRR, verified with traffic streams through FRR.
425: +
426: +## Known issues and limitations
427: +
428: +* containerlab links have an MTU of 9500 by default, while BNG Blaster network interfaces use an MTU of 1500 by default and IS-IS accepts PDUs of up to 1497 bytes. Routers size IS-IS PDUs to the link MTU, for example padded hellos, and depending on the implementation LSPs and CSNPs, which are then rejected, so that the adjacency does not come up or the database is incomplete. Either configure `jumbo-frames`, the `mtu` of the interface and the IS-IS `max-pdu-size` of the BNG Blaster according to the link MTU, as in the [IS-IS lab example](../../lab-examples/bngblaster02.md) (requires BNG Blaster 1.2.0 or newer), or set the [`mtu`](../topo-def-file.md#links) of links to routing peers to 1500.
429: +* Without `"interfaces": {"jumbo-frames": true}` in the BNG Blaster configuration, frames larger than about 4 KB are not received completely.
430: +
431: +## Contact
432: +
433: +The kind is maintained by RtBrick, contact <bngblaster@rtbrick.com>.

+---\n296: +search:\n297: +  boost: 4\n298: +kind_code_name: rtbrick_bngblaster\n299: +kind_display_name: RtBrick BNG Blaster\n300: +---\n301: +# -{{ kind_display_name }}-\n302: +\n303: +[-{{ kind_display_name }}-](https://github.com/rtbrick/bngblaster) is an open-source network tester for access and routing protocols. It emulates subscribers (PPPoE, IPoE, L2TP, IPTV) and routing protocols (IS-IS, OSPF, LDP, BGP including EVPN), and verifies millions of traffic streams. -{{ kind_display_name }}- node is identified with the `-{{ kind_code_name }}-` kind in the [topology file](../topo-def-file.md); `bngblaster` is accepted as a short alias.\n304: +\n305: +The container image runs the [BNG Blaster controller](https://github.com/rtbrick/bngblaster-controller), which manages the test instances and provides a REST API and web UI. Version 1.1.1 or newer of the controller is required, which is part of the image since BNG Blaster 1.1.0. The image `ghcr.io/rtbrick/bngblaster:1.2.0` or newer is recommended.\n306: +\n307: +## Getting -{{ kind_display_name }}- image\n308: +\n309: +The image is publicly available in the GitHub Container Registry as [`ghcr.io/rtbrick/bngblaster`](https://github.com/rtbrick/bngblaster/pkgs/container/bngblaster). It is used by default if the node has no `image` configured.\n310: +\n311: +```bash\n312: +docker pull ghcr.io/rtbrick/bngblaster:latest\n313: +```\n314: +\n315: +## Managing -{{ kind_display_name }}- nodes\n316: +\n317: +/// tab | Web UI and REST API\n318: +The controller serves a web UI and REST API on port 8001, from the lab host for example at `http://clab-<lab-name>-<node-name>:8001`. To reach it from a remote browser, publish the port with a different host port per node:\n319: +\n320: +```yaml\n321: +    bngblaster:\n322: +      kind: rtbrick_bngblaster\n323: +      ports:\n324: +        - 8001:8001\n325: +```\n326: +\n327: +///\n328: +\n329: +/// tab | CLI\n330: +`bngblaster-cli` sends commands to the control socket of the running test:\n331: +\n332: +```bash\n333: +docker exec -it clab-<lab-name>-<node-name> \\\n334: +  bngblaster-cli /var/bngblaster/clab/run.sock session-counters\n335: +```\n336: +\n337: +///\n338: +\n339: +/// tab | Shell\n340: +```bash\n341: +docker exec -it clab-<lab-name>-<node-name> bash\n342: +```\n343: +\n344: +///\n345: +\n346: +## Interface naming\n347: +\n348: +-{{ kind_display_name }}- uses the interface names of the links as they are, which are referenced in the BNG Blaster configuration:\n349: +\n350: +* `eth0` - management interface connected to the containerlab management network\n351: +* `eth1+` - data interfaces, any other name can be used as well\n352: +\n353: +## Features and options\n354: +\n355: +### Startup configuration\n356: +\n357: +With the [`startup-config`](../nodes.md#startup-config) property, a user sets the path to a BNG Blaster configuration file (JSON). It is copied to `/var/bngblaster/clab/config.json` in the container, and the controller starts this test instance (`clab`) automatically once all links of the node are attached.\n358: +\n359: +```yaml\n360: +topology:\n361: +  nodes:\n362: +    bngblaster:\n363: +      kind: rtbrick_bngblaster\n364: +      startup-config: pppoe.json\n365: +```\n366: +\n367: +Without a startup-config, or with [`suppress-startup-config`](../nodes.md#suppress-startup-config), only the controller is started, and tests are created and started through the web UI or REST API.\n368: +\n369: +As for other kinds, an existing `config.json` from a previous deployment is kept, so changes to the startup-config file take effect only after `containerlab destroy --cleanup`, with `containerlab deploy --reconfigure`, or with [`enforce-startup-config`](../nodes.md#enforce-startup-config) set for the node.\n370: +\n371: +The start arguments of the test, for example to write a report or log file, are read from `/var/bngblaster/clab/run.json` if present:\n372: +\n373: +```yaml\n374: +      binds:\n375: +        - run.json:/var/bngblaster/clab/run.json:ro\n376: +```\n377: +\n378: +```json\n379: +{\n380: +    \"report\": true,\n381: +    \"report_flags\": [\"sessions\", \"streams\"],\n382: +    \"logging\": true,\n383: +    \"logging_flags\": [\"info\", \"error\"]\n384: +}\n385: +```\n386: +\n387: +### Results\n388: +\n389: +The node's lab directory (`clab-<lab-name>/<node-name>`) is mounted as `/var/bngblaster`, the instance directory of the controller. The configuration, logs and the report of the test (`clab/run_report.json`) are kept there after the lab is destroyed, unless the lab directory is removed with `containerlab destroy --cleanup` or `containerlab deploy --reconfigure`.\n390: +\n391: +### Stopping the test\n392: +\n393: +The controller stops the test when the container is stopped, and BNG Blaster writes the report in all of the following cases:\n394: +\n395: +* `containerlab destroy`, with or without `--graceful`, and the removal of the node by `containerlab apply`: the node is stopped before any link or node of the lab is removed, also those of the device under test, so that BNG Blaster tears down its sessions gracefully (PPPoE: LCP Terminate-Request and PADT; routing sessions are closed). A teardown that takes longer than 30 seconds is ended at once, still with the report. For large tests, where the device under test should see every session closed, raise `BNGBLASTERCTRL_STOP_TIMEOUT` (e.g. `5m`) and the containerlab [`--timeout`](../../cmd/deploy.md#timeout) (default 2 minutes) to more than that plus 10 seconds, e.g. `containerlab destroy --timeout 6m`.\n396: +\n397: +* `containerlab stop`: the links are removed before the node is stopped, so the sessions can not be torn down gracefully. The controller detects the missing interfaces and stops the test at once.\n398: +* The test ends by itself or is stopped through the web UI, REST API or `bngblaster-cli`.\n399: +\n400: +`containerlab start` and `containerlab restart` start the test again once all links are attached. This removes the results of the previous run, so copy them before if needed.\n401: +\n402: +### Health check\n403: +\n404: +The node has a default health check, which is healthy while the test is running or after it finished without error, and unhealthy while waiting for the links, while the test starts, or if it failed. Other nodes can therefore wait for the test with [`wait-for`](../nodes.md#stages) and the `healthy` stage. The check is replaced by a [`healthcheck`](../nodes.md#healthcheck) configured for the node.\n405: +\n406: +### Environment variables\n407: +\n408: +The kind sets the following controller variables, which can be overridden with the node's `env`:\n409: +\n410: +| Variable                         | Description                                          | Default                            |\n411: +| -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |\n412: +| `BNGBLASTERCTRL_AUTOSTART`       | Instance started automatically                        | `clab` if a startup-config is set  |\n413: +| `BNGBLASTERCTRL_WAIT_INTERFACES` | Number of interfaces to wait for before the start     | number of links of the node        |\n414: +\n415: +All other controller options are available as `BNGBLASTERCTRL_<OPTION>` variables as well, for example `BNGBLASTERCTRL_STOP_TIMEOUT` (default `30s`) for the graceful teardown when the node is stopped, see the [controller documentation](https://github.com/rtbrick/bngblaster-controller).\n416: +\n417: +### IPv6\n418: +\n419: +The kind sets the sysctl `net.ipv6.conf.default.disable_ipv6=1`, so that the kernel does not use IPv6 on the data interfaces, which BNG Blaster handles itself. The management interface keeps IPv6. The sysctl is not set with `network-mode: host` or `network-mode: container:<name>`, where the node has no network namespace of its own.\n420: +\n421: +## Lab examples\n422: +\n423: +* [BNG Blaster PPPoE](../../lab-examples/bngblaster01.md) - PPPoE server and clients emulated back to back by one BNG Blaster node.\n424: +* [BNG Blaster and FRR IS-IS](../../lab-examples/bngblaster02.md) - emulated IS-IS topology advertised to FRR, verified with traffic streams through FRR.\n425: +\n426: +## Known issues and limitations\n427: +\n428: +* containerlab links have an MTU of 9500 by default, while BNG Blaster network interfaces use an MTU of 1500 by default and IS-IS accepts PDUs of up to 1497 bytes. Routers size IS-IS PDUs to the link MTU, for example padded hellos, and depending on the implementation LSPs and CSNPs, which are then rejected, so that the adjacency does not come up or the database is incomplete. Either configure `jumbo-frames`, the `mtu` of the interface and the IS-IS `max-pdu-size` of the BNG Blaster according to the link MTU, as in the [IS-IS lab example](../../lab-examples/bngblaster02.md) (requires BNG Blaster 1.2.0 or newer), or set the [`mtu`](../topo-def-file.md#links) of links to routing peers to 1500.\n429: +* Without `\"interfaces\": {\"jumbo-frames\": true}` in the BNG Blaster configuration, frames larger than about 4 KB are not received completely.\n430: +\n431: +## Contact\n432: +\n433: +The kind is maintained by RtBrick, contact <bngblaster@rtbrick.com>.\n434: diff --git a/lab-examples/bngblaster01/bngblaster01.clab.yml b/lab-examples/bngblaster01/bngblaster01.clab.yml\n\n(Showing lines 185-434 of 1460. FRR learns the routes to all emulated routers.\n+\n+Two traffic streams are sent from the second BNG Blaster interface `eth2` to the loopback addresses of the emulated routers `node1` (192.168.0.0) and `node20` (192.168.0.11). FRR routes them back to the BNG Blaster on `eth1`, which verifies the streams for loss. The packets sent before FRR installed the routes, usually within a few seconds after the start, are not received.\n+\n+```\n+bngblaster eth1 <---- IS-IS adjacency ----> eth1 frr\n+bngblaster eth2 ---- traffic streams -----> eth2 frr\n+```\n+\n+The test starts automatically once both links are attached.\n+\n+## Use cases\n+\n+The IS-IS database and routes of FRR:\n+\n+```bash\n+docker exec clab-bngblaster02-frr vtysh -c \"show isis database\"\n+docker exec clab-bngblaster02-frr vtysh -c \"show ip route isis\"\n+```\n+\n+The adjacency and the traffic streams on the BNG Blaster:\n+\n+```bash\n+docker exec clab-bngblaster02-bngblaster \\\n+  bngblaster-cli /var/bngblaster/clab/run.sock isis-adjacencies\n+docker exec clab-bngblaster02-bngblaster \\\n+  bngblaster-cli /var/bngblaster/clab/run.sock stream-summary\n+```\n+\n+When the lab is destroyed, the BNG Blaster is stopped first, withdraws its IS-IS topology and closes the adjacency before FRR and the links are removed, and the stream results are written to `clab-bngblaster02/bngblaster/clab/run_report.json`.\n+\n+FRR pads its IS-IS hellos to the interface MTU, which is 9500 for containerlab links by default, and sizes its CSNP and PSNP according to it as well. `isis.json` therefore enables `jumbo-frames`, sets the `mtu` of `eth1` to 9500 and raises the IS-IS `max-pdu-size` to 9497 (MTU minus 3 bytes for the LLC header). IS-IS PDUs larger than 1497 bytes are sent as LLC in Ethernet II frames with ethertype 0x8870, see [IS-IS jumbo frames](https://rtbrick.github.io/bngblaster/routing/isis.html#jumbo-frames). This requires BNG Blaster 1.2.0 or newer.\n+\n+[topofile]: https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/tree/main/lab-examples/bngblaster02/bngblaster02.clab.yml\n+\n+[^1]: Resource requirements are provisional. The check is replaced by a [`healthcheck`](../nodes.md#healthcheck) configured for the node.\n+\n+### Environment variables\n+\n+The kind sets the following controller variables, which can be overridden with the node's `env`:\n+\n+| Variable                         | Description                                          | Default                            |\n+| -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |\n+| `BNGBLASTERCTRL_AUTOSTART`       | Instance started automatically                        | `clab` if a startup-config is set  |\n+| `BNGBLASTERCTRL_WAIT_INTERFACES` | Number of interfaces to wait for before the start     | number of links of the node        |\n+\n+All other controller options are available as `BNGBLASTERCTRL_<OPTION>` variables as well, for example `BNGBLASTERCTRL_STOP_TIMEOUT` (default `30s`) for the graceful teardown when the node is stopped, see the [controller documentation](https://github.com/rtbrick/bngblaster-controller).\n+\n+### IPv6\n+\n+The kind sets the sysctl `net.ipv6.conf.default.disable_ipv6=1`, so that the kernel does not use IPv6 on the data interfaces, which BNG Blaster handles itself. The management interface keeps IPv6. The sysctl is not set with `network-mode: host` or `network-mode: container:<name>`, where the node has no network namespace of its own.\n+\n+## Lab examples\n+\n+* [BNG Blaster PPPoE](../../lab-examples/bngblaster01.md) - PPPoE server and clients emulated back to back by one BNG Blaster node.\n+* [BNG Blaster and FRR IS-IS](../../lab-examples/bngblaster02.md) - emulated IS-IS topology advertised to FRR, verified with traffic streams through FRR.\n+\n+## Known issues and limitations\n+\n+* containerlab links have an MTU of 9500 by default, while BNG Blaster network interfaces use an MTU of 1500 by default and IS-IS accepts PDUs of up to 1497 bytes. Routers size IS-IS PDUs to the link MTU, for example padded hellos, and depending on the implementation LSPs and CSNPs, which are then rejected, so that the adjacency does not come up or the database is incomplete. Either configure `jumbo-frames`, the `mtu` of the interface and the IS-IS `max-pdu-size` of the BNG Blaster according to the link MTU, as in the [IS-IS lab example](../../lab-examples/bngblaster02.md) (requires BNG Blaster 1.2.0 or newer), or set the [`mtu`](../topo-def-file.md#links) of links to routing peers to 1500.\n+* Without `\"interfaces\": {\"jumbo-frames\": true}` in the BNG Blaster configuration, frames larger than about 4 KB are not received completely.\n+\n+## Contact\n+\n+The kind is maintained by RtBrick, contact <bngblaster@rtbrick.com>.\ndiff --git a/lab-examples/bngblaster01/bngblaster01.clab.yml b/lab-examples/bngblaster01/bngblaster01.clab.yml",

No — `Start` just starts the container; the env `BNGBLASTERCTRL_WAIT_INTERFACES` persists in the container config (env is part of container creation). On `stop`, links are parked (removed from netns) and on `start` restored. So when the container restarts, the env `BNGBLASTERCTRL_WAIT_INTERFACES=N` is still set from deploy time, and the controller waits for N interfaces again. That works. OK.

But what about `containerlab deploy --reconfigure` or apply recreate? Deploy runs again. Fine.

Now what about the apply flow (reconcile)? If links change (added) via `containerlab apply`, `Deploy` runs again with new endpoint count? envWaitInterfaces is only `setDefault` — the first value set at initial deploy time stays because env map in Cfg persists? In apply, the node config is rebuilt from the topology file and a new node is created via Init (no envWaitInterfaces — that's only set in Deploy, not persisted to topology). Then Deploy runs on recreate with the new count. OK.

But hold on — `Deploy` uses `setDefault(n.Cfg.Env, envWaitInterfaces, ...)`: if the user deployed with 2 links, then `apply` adds a third link with LinkApplyModeRecreate → node recreated, Init called fresh (env has only user keys + autostart), Deploy sets 3. Good.

Docker healthcheck test format: ["CMD", ...] or ["CMD-SHELL", ...]. Let me check the docker runtime conversion. Reasoning
Confirmed: `preDestroyNodes` runs before `CleanupFilteredLinks` and `deleteNodes`. The doc's ordering claims hold for destroy.

Now — an important detail about `PreDestroy` blocking behavior: `preDestroyNodes` runs concurrently across nodes with `maxWorkers`. The docker `StopContainer` uses `d.config.Timeout` (default 2 minutes per docs). During destroy, the CLab copy gets `WithTimeout(c.timeout)` — the `--timeout` flag. So the stop waits up to the timeout. Doc says raise `--timeout`. Consistent.

However — one issue: `preDestroyNodes` uses `maxWorkers` (default workers count). Each node's PreDestroy blocks up to timeout concurrently. For destroy of a lab with bngblaster + other nodes, all concurrent, fine.

But wait — a subtle correctness issue in PreDestroy: it calls `n.GetContainerStatus(ctx) == clabruntime.Running`. GetContainerStatus via DefaultNode: let me check — it calls `d.Runtime.GetContainerStatus(ctx, d.GetContainerName())`. If the container doesn't exist (NotFound), returns NotFound. OK.

Next checkpoint: apply flow. `deleteApplyNodes` at line 635: `c.preDestroyNodes(ctx, hookNodes, 0)` — hookNodes presumably only the nodes being deleted. OK — doc says "the removal of the node by `containerlab apply`: the node is stopped before any link or node of the lab is removed". Hmm — in the apply case, `deleteApplyNodes` calls preDestroyNodes with only hookNodes (the nodes being removed). If a bngblaster node is NOT being removed but a peer link is being removed... then PreDestroy doesn't run for the bngblaster, so the bngblaster isn't stopped before its links are removed. But that's an edge case (apply removing links of a kept bngblaster node) — the doc claim says "the removal of the node by containerlab apply" — i.e., when the bngblaster node itself is removed. That's accurate. Fine.

Wait, one more: in the apply case with a kept node and changed links — LinkApplyMode default is Recreate → the bngblaster node is recreated (deleted + created). deleteApplyNodes deletes the bngblaster node too → preDestroyNodes includes it (hookNodes = nodes being deleted). Let me quickly check line 620-640.

9. `Deploy` — `envWaitInterfaces` set via `setDefault` only when `n.Cfg.Env[envAutostart] != ""`. If user set autostart to a different instance name... whatever, fine.

10. Also check `clab generate` support: `generateable=true`, `generateIfFormat="eth%d"` — the node allows arbitrary names though ("access1", "network1"). Hmm — the generate format `eth%d` is only used by `containerlab generate` to produce interface names. Not conflicting with CheckInterfaceName allowing any name. Fine.

11. Check the `bngblaster` alias vs `rtbrick_bngblaster`: kind enum includes both; docs say alias accepted. Fine.

12. Robot test: `${lab-dir} ${CURDIR}/clab-${lab-name}` — when tests run, lab is deployed in the tests dir. `Get File ${lab-dir}/pppoe/clab/config.json` — LabDir bind. OK.

13. One potential real issue: the healthcheck `StartPeriod: 300` — 5 minutes. `docker inspect .State.Health.Status` returns "starting" during start period — `Node Is Healthy` waits 120s for status == healthy. If the test waits for links... links are attached quickly (deploy attaches links right after start). OK.

14. Now — the one thing I flagged earlier: `PreDestroy` calls `n.Runtime.StopContainer(ctx, ...)`. For podman runtime — check podman's StopContainer exists with same semantics (timeout config). Presumably. Fine.

15. The `deploy.go:991` line: `node.Config().Binds = append(node.Config().Binds, ...)` — some late-added bind (probably node cert dir). Not relevant.

Reasoning
Important discovery about `suppress-startup-config` + the bngblaster `PreDeploy`:

`PreDeploy` in bngblaster calls `clabutils.CreateDirectory(path.Dir(n.Cfg.ResStartupConfig), ...)` unconditionally (when StartupConfig != ""), then reads StartupConfig and calls `GenerateConfig`. `GenerateConfig` returns early (no-op) when `SuppressStartupConfig` is set — so the config is NOT written. That's consistent with the Init logic (no autostart env since config.json won't exist). Fine.

`enforce-startup-config`: `GenerateConfig` regenerates when EnforceStartupConfig is set. Good — the frr-style flow is honored.

One more subtlety in PreDeploy: `os.ReadFile(n.Cfg.StartupConfig)` reads and templates via `GenerateConfig`'s `SubstituteEnvsAndTemplateWithEnv`. If the user's config contains `{{ }}` templating — intended feature. If a user's JSON contains `{{` accidentally... same as other kinds. Fine.

Edge: `VerifyStartupConfig` default — checks file exists (resolved). Good, error caught pre-deploy via CheckDeploymentConditions.

Now, one more possible issue in PreDeploy: it ignores `params` entirely (named `_`), skipping `LoadOrGenerateCertificate` and `SSHPubKeys`. `SSHPubKeys` is only frr-specific (write via PostDeploy). Certificate is generic node option: `certificate` key in node-config schema (line ~?). For bngblaster, setting `certificate: my-cert` would have no effect — silently. Compare ciena_saos — let me check whether ciena's PreDeploy calls cert... Actually the finding: `DefaultNode.PreDeploy` handles cert; kinds overriding PreDeploy should call `n.DefaultNode.PreDeploy` (as VRNode.PreDeploy does — mikrotik calls `n.VRNode.PreDeploy(ctx, params)`; frr calls LoadOrGenerateCertificate directly). bngblaster does neither. P4 severity — the `certificate` node option is generic and documented; for this kind it silently does nothing. Impact: user configures cert for e.g. DTLS/BGP-TLS in test config; expects containerlab CA flow; nothing happens. Suggested fix: call `n.DefaultNode.PreDeploy(ctx, params)` at the start of the override (which does the cert step), or at minimum `LoadOrGenerateCertificate`.

Wait — actually there's more: does cert loading affect the `SshConfig`/mgmt? No. Only `Cfg.Certificate` usage. It's a niche option. P4.

Next: check whether `deploy.go` around line 991 adds a bind that might interact. Not needed.

Now — one more look at a potential real correctness issue: the `Deploy` override and `LinkApplyModeRestart`. On `apply` with link changes and mode restart: the container is stopped, links added, container restarted. Deploy isn't called; env WAIT_INTERFACES keeps the old count. If a link was added, the controller would wait for the old count only. Docs say the test starts once "all links are attached" — with restart-apply the count is stale. But default LinkApplyMode for this kind is Recreate (ImageLinkApplyMode default) → Deploy runs again. Restart mode requires explicit opt-in via `link-apply-mode: restart`. Minor edge; probably not worth a finding, or maybe a note. Hmm. Actually — wait: does the kind declare LinkApplyMode? No override → `LinkApplyModeRecreate` default (or image-based live?). `ImageLinkApplyMode(ctx, LinkApplyModeRecreate)` — checks image labels for live support. bngblaster image has no such label → Recreate. So on link changes the node is recreated, Deploy runs, fresh env count. OK — no finding. Not even worth a coverage note maybe; I'll mention in notes.

Also `containerlab deploy` on an already-running lab → error "already been deployed". `containerlab redeploy`? That destroys and deploys. OK.

What about `restart` of the node via `containerlab restart` (not full redeploy)? `Start` restarts the container; env persists (stored in container config at creation). Endpoint count unchanged. OK.

Now — `PreDestroy` and `Stop`: `DefaultNode.Stop` — does it call PreDestroy? No — PreDestroy is destroy/apply only. On `stop`, links parked first then StopContainer — docs correctly describe. Consistent.

What about `deploy --reconfigure`: destroy of the single node? `reconfigure` = destroy lab + deploy. Deploy sets env again. OK.

Let me also double-check `GetContainerStatus` for bngblaster `PreDestroy` — with mock runtime test passing `GetContainerStatus` returning status for name... fine.

Also check podman's StopContainer signature to ensure `n.StopSignal` empty is fine in podman too:
