Reasoning
Podman StopContainer handles empty signal fine (default SIGTERM).

One more check — the `Node` config `Stopsignal` field and the topology `stopsignal`? Not relevant.

Now — one more potential finding to examine: in `Init`, when `n.Cfg.SuppressStartupConfig` is true AND `ResStartupConfig` is set — PreDeploy still creates `LabDir/clab` directory. Harmless.

And — `Deploy` env check `n.Cfg.Env[envAutostart] != ""`: what if the user overrides `BNGBLASTERCTRL_AUTOSTART: "false"` or empty to disable? Setting `"false"` (non-empty) would still set WAIT_INTERFACES — but that's user's explicit env; the controller interprets. Edge, fine.

Now `healthcheck` port 8001 — the kind doesn't expose REST port by default; docs show publishing via ports. Fine.

Next: check docs claim "The check is replaced by a healthcheck configured for the node" — code: `if n.Cfg.Healthcheck == nil` — yes, replaced. Fine.

Docs claim about `containerlab start`: "`containerlab start` and `containerlab restart` start the test again once all links are attached" — via env in container config. OK.

Now, one thing I should verify: `Test: []string{"CMD", "/usr/bin/bngblasterctrl", "-health"}` — the path `/usr/bin/bngblasterctrl` must exist in the image. Can't verify image contents — external. The doc says controller ≥1.1.1 / image ≥1.1.0. DefaultImage is `:latest` so fine. Can't verify — coverage note.

Also — `StartPeriod: 300` with `Interval 5, Timeout 3, Retries 3`: robot `Node Is Healthy` waits `Wait Until Keyword Succeeds 120s 2s` — if health stays "starting" for the full 300s start period... wait, during start period, health status is "starting" but the check still runs. The comment says "unhealthy while the controller waits for the links (up to 5 minutes), which the start period covers". During start period, failed checks don't count towards unhealthy — status shows "starting". So `Node Is Healthy` waits until the test actually runs → healthy. In the robot lab, links attach in seconds, so healthy within 120s. OK.

But hmm — one important interplay: healthcheck `CMD /usr/bin/bngblasterctrl -health` — is `bngblasterctrl` at `/usr/bin/`? The docs say CLI is `bngblaster-cli` (different tool). Can't verify externally; note it.

Now let me double check `IsHealthy` used by `wait-for: healthy` stage — DefaultNode.IsHealthy inspects container health. Fine.

Let me now check `manifest.json` fully for the complete path list, to make sure I haven't missed any changed file (e.g., a tests/16 or others).

Reasoning
The veth deployment code doesn't reject same-node links: `deployAEnd` deploys endpoint A into the node's netns, `deployBEnd` deploys endpoint B into the same node's netns (via `AddLinkToContainer`, which is idempotent per link — it uses `ExecFunction` to enter the node netns and moves the link). Both halves of the veth pair end up in the same container netns as eth1/eth2. No validation rejects same-node links. So the lab examples' `bngblaster:eth1-bngblaster:eth2` loopback-style link is supported by the existing veth machinery.

Wait — one thing to double check: `AddLinkToContainer` for docker — when both A and B ends belong to the same node, does the docker runtime handle it? `AddLinkToContainer` in docker runtime enters the container netns and moves the link. Yes, it should work; this pattern (link between two interfaces of the same node) is a known containerlab capability used by e.g. CSR-style topologies... Actually I'm not 100% sure, but the code path clearly supports it: no guard against it, and both ends are moved independently. Also `HasSameNodeAndInterface` is about duplicates (eth1-eth1 same node), which is rejected — the examples use eth1/eth2, different interfaces. Fine.

## Review: `rtbrick_bngblaster` node kind

This PR adds a new `rtbrick_bngblaster` node kind (BNG Blaster traffic generator), with unit tests, a CI integration test, docs, lab examples, workflow wiring, and schema entries. The implementation is well-scoped and reuses existing machinery (`DefaultNode` embedding, generic binds/healthcheck plumbing, standard deploy/destroy flow). I traced the destroy/apply flow, docker and podman `StopContainer` handling of the zero-value stop signal, startup-config path resolution, bind resolution, `CheckInterfaceName` behavior, same-node veth link deployment, and the schema structure. Most claims in the new kind docs check out against the code. I found two actionable issues.

| Priority | Title |
|---|---|
| P3 | Schema lacks `topology.kinds` entries for `rtbrick_bngblaster`/`bngblaster` despite `additionalProperties: false` |
| P4 | `PreDeploy` skips `LoadOrGenerateCertificate`, silently ignoring the `certificate` node option |

### Findings

**P3 — Schema lacks `topology.kinds` entries for `rtbrick_bngblaster`/`bngblaster` despite `additionalProperties: false`**

- Location: [schemas/clab.schema.json#L4004-L4035](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/fbd18ce0b2e7b230c501440b513189c8e7422441/schemas/clab.schema.json#L4004-L4035) (head)
- Problem: The PR adds `rtbrick_bngblaster` and `bngblaster` to the kind enum and to `topology.nodes` definitions, but not to the `topology.kinds` properties section, which closes with `"additionalProperties": false`. The PR's own test topology uses kind-level config at [tests/17-rtbrick-bngblaster/01-bngblaster.clab.yml#L4-L5](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/fbd18ce0b2e7b230c501440b513189c8e7422441/tests/17-rtbrick-bngblaster/01-bngblaster.clab.yml#L4-L5).
- Trigger: A user writes `topology.kinds.rtbrick_bngblaster:` in a topology and validates it with any tooling that consumes `schemas/clab.schema.json` (editor validation, CI schema checks). The PR's shipped test topology itself triggers this.
- Impact: Valid configurations are flagged as invalid by schema-aware tooling; the new kind cannot be used at kind level without a validation error.
- Correction: Add `rtbrick_bngblaster` and `bngblaster` property entries under `topology.kinds`, mirroring the shape used in the `topology.nodes` additions (`allOf` referencing `node-config` plus `kind-specific-config-other`). Note: `veesix_osvbng`, `spirent_stc`, and `ostinato` are also missing from the kinds section, so this is a pre-existing pattern of omission — but this PR adds a new instance of it, and its own test file depends on the missing entry.

**P4 — `PreDeploy` skips `LoadOrGenerateCertificate`, silently ignoring the `certificate` node option**

- Location: [nodes/rtbrick_bngblaster/rtbrick_bngblaster.go#L116-L133](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/fbd18ce0b2e7b230c501440b513189c8e7422441/nodes/rtbrick_bngblaster/rtbrick_bngblaster.go#L116-L133) (head)
- Problem: The `bngblaster` `PreDeploy` override neither calls `n.DefaultNode.PreDeploy` (whose only action is `LoadOrGenerateCertificate`, `nodes/default_node.go:119-128`) nor calls `LoadOrGenerateCertificate` explicitly. Comparable kinds retain it: `frr` calls it in its own override (`nodes/frr/frr.go:183`), and `mikrotik_chr` calls `VRNode.PreDeploy`.
- Trigger: A user sets the generic per-node `certificate:` option on a bngblaster node.
- Impact: The option is silently ignored — no node certificate is generated or loaded, with no warning or error.
- Correction: Call `LoadOrGenerateCertificate` in the override (as `frr` does). This is safe for this root-namespace-based kind: `LoadOrGenerateCertificate` early-returns `nil` when `Cfg.Certificate` is unset or `Issue` is false (`nodes/default_node.go:894-897`), so it is a no-op unless the user opts in.

### Verified non-issues (noted for confidence)

- `PreDestroy` passing the zero-value `StopSignal` is safe: docker and podman `StopContainer` both default to `SIGTERM` with the configured timeout when the signal is empty.
- Docs claims about `PreDestroy` running before link removal are accurate for both the destroy flow (`core/destroy.go:470-481`) and the apply/recreate flow (`deleteApplyNodes`).
- The `LabDir` bind appended in `Init` is unaffected by `resolveBindPaths` (which only checks user-supplied binds at config load), and `PreDeploy` creates the lab directory first.
- The healthcheck `["CMD", ...]` format passes straight through to docker's `container.HealthConfig.Test` and is valid.
- Same-node veth links (`bngblaster:eth1-bngblaster:eth2`) are supported by the veth deployment code; only duplicate node+interface pairs are rejected.
- `CheckInterfaceName` correctly rejects `eth0` except under `network-mode: none`.
- Workflow job patterns, robot keywords, `mkdocs.yml` nav entries, and lab example files (including matching frr image tag and referenced bind files) are all consistent with existing conventions.
- Unit tests cover `Init` defaults, startup-config autostart, and user healthcheck/bind overrides.

### Coverage notes

- All 26 changed paths from `diff.txt`/`manifest.json` were reviewed, including workflows, schema, docs, lab examples, node implementation, and tests, plus surrounding code: destroy/apply flow, docker/podman runtime stop paths, `DefaultNode` helpers, config resolution, and link deployment.
- Source-only review: no tests, formatters, or CI were executed. Image-internal details (the healthcheck binary path `/usr/bin/bngblasterctrl`, bngblaster CLI semantics) cannot be verified from the repo; the robot test's `Node Is Healthy` step exercises the healthcheck in CI.
- I did not verify whether the containerlab runtime itself enforces `schemas/clab.schema.json` at runtime; the P3 impact is stated for schema-aware tooling and editors, which is the schema's documented purpose.
